get.description:
The projected spend by month against the stored purchase budgets.

Read-only.  ``committed_spend`` is every site group's projected
supply value of the month, ``planned_spend`` its planned receipts
value and ``total_spend`` the two together; ``budget`` is the
stored budget of the month (null without one), ``remaining`` the
budget minus the total spend and ``over_budget`` true only when a
budget exists and the total spend exceeds it.  422 when
``as_of`` is after the current server date or when ``months`` is
outside 1 to 12 inclusive, and 422 when a given lever is out of
range (``service_level`` must be a number strictly between 0 and
1, each multiplier a positive finite number) or a scaled input
overflows the reorder formula.

The deferral candidates of the over-budget months of the horizon.

Read-only, no pagination: every candidate of the requested
month(s) comes back in a single response.  For each month the
spend view flags over budget, the planned orders arriving in the
month are ordered with the orders that would not stock out first,
by cover descending then value descending, then the stock-out ones
by cover descending, and suggested in that order while the
suggested value is still below the overrun — an order that would
stock out, or has value 0, is never suggested; a deferral is
estimated one month at a time and later months are not re-planned.
422 when ``as_of`` is after the current server date or when
``months`` is outside 1 to 12 inclusive, and 422 when a given
lever is out of range (``service_level`` must be a number strictly

post.description:
Preview or confirm the release of one month's planned orders.

Preview (``confirm`` false or absent, any signed-in user): the
plan of ``plan_release(month)`` with ``acumatica_available`` false
and null outcomes and codes when the Acumatica configuration is
incomplete (no client call), otherwise
``preview_draft_purchase_orders`` called once and each group's
``outcome``, ``warehouse_code``, ``vendor_code``, ``order_nbr`` and
``error`` copied from the per-order results; an Acumatica auth or
transport failure is 502.  422 for a bad month or a
``plan_release`` ``ValueError``.

Confirm (``confirm`` true), checked in order with nothing written
to Acumatica before every check passes: a non-admin gets 403
(``require_admin``); the whole release then holds the PostgreSQL
advisory lock on its own connection (a second confirm while one is
running gets 409), released in a ``finally`` so the guarantee holds
across several API worker processes; incomplete Acumatica
configuration gets 503; switched-off writes get 409 saying writes
are off.  Otherwise one ``pending`` ``plan_releases`` row per
group is written (the caller's username as actor, the group's
exact lines), ``create_draft_purchase_orders`` is called once with
every group — the drafts are created on hold, committing the spend
still requires releasing the hold under Acumatica's own approval
process — and each row is updated to the group's outcome
(``created``, ``exists`` or ``error``) with its order number, codes
and error, returning the plan with each group's outcome.  An
Acumatica auth or transport failure that aborts the batch is 502
and marks the release's rows ``aborted``, so the audit always shows
every release attempt.  An ``exists`` outcome is refused — 409, the
group's row ``error`` — when the current plan's lines differ from
the stored
snapshot of the same origin — a difference of rounding alone is
not a difference, the stored line's ``unit_cost`` and ``value``
are rounded the same half-up way before the comparison — so a
changed plan is never reported as already bought.  A confirm with no releasable groups is
200 with empty groups and calls Acumatica not at all.

get.description:
Every stored release row, newest first; admin only.

ADMIN-ONLY, checked via ``require_admin`` exactly like the confirm:
a signed-in non-admin is refused with 403 and without a token with
401.  Rows are ordered by ``created_at DESC, id DESC`` so equal
timestamps list deterministically, and every column of the row is
returned (``created_at`` and ``updated_at`` as ISO-8601).

get.description:
Where the released plan POs stand in Acumatica, as of today.

Open to any signed-in user behind the mount-time gate, like the
release preview (the admin-only audit route stays admin only).
The newest ``plan_releases`` row per released order number —
outcomes ``created`` and ``exists`` with an order number — is
read from Acumatica in one session and classified as of today:
the orders come back sorted by state priority (``late`` first,
then ``awaiting_approval``, ``partially_received``, ``open``,
``received``, ``cancelled``, ``missing``) then oldest release
first, with the fixed counts keys ``awaiting_approval``,
``late``, ``partly_received`` and ``received``.  With nothing
released the answer is 200 with no orders and zero counts — and
no Acumatica call — taking precedence over the 503; incomplete
Acumatica configuration otherwise gets 503 and an Acumatica auth
or transport failure 502, with no partial results of a failed
read ever merged into the answer.  Nothing is written.

Every order line in the response carries ``item_description`` —

Every order also carries ``expected_on`` and

Open to any signed-in user (the router is mounted behind the

get.description:
The DDMRP buffer zones of every designated item-site.

Open to any authenticated user (the router is mounted behind the
app's authentication gate).  As of the demand statistics' default
as-of date (``app.stats.demand.default_as_of``), one row per
stored designation, ordered by item_code then site_code: the ADU
is the sum of the pair's ``demand_events.quantity`` in the
``ddmrp.adu_window_days`` days ending on that date, divided by
that number of days (a non-integer window is used whole, never
truncated); the DLT is the item's pooled observed lead
time in days (``dlt_source`` "observed") or, when the item has no
observation in the window, the item-site's
``item_sites.master_lead_time_days`` (``dlt_source`` "master");
the demand class and the coefficient of variation (the square
root of the statistics' cv2, null when it is null) come from the
demand statistics and the order cycle days from the item-site's
recommended order quantity (null when it has none).  The status
is "no_demand" when the ADU is 0 or the pair has no demand
statistics, "no_lead_time" when neither DLT source exists and
"ok" otherwise; only the "ok" rows carry the zone fields of
``app.ddmrp.zones.buffer_zones``, the others carry null zone
fields.  Every statistic is read once per call, whatever the
number of rows, and nothing is written.

The DDMRP plan of every designated item-site with an "ok" zone row.

Open to any authenticated user (the router is mounted behind the
app's authentication gate).  As of the demand statistics' default
as-of date, builds the zone rows with the same shared code
``GET /api/ddmrp/zones`` uses (``ddmrp_zone_rows``), keeps the
"ok" rows and enriches each with the pair's ``on_hand`` quantity
(0 with the note "no on-hand record; treated as 0" when the pair
has none), its ``open_supply`` (the sum of the ``open_units`` of
its ``open_purchase_lines`` rows with ``open_units`` above 0 whose
``promised_on`` is null or no more than 90 days before the as-of
date, future dates included; the note "<n> stale open purchase
lines excluded" when any line is excluded), its
``qualified_demand`` (0, with the note "no open sales-order
demand in the feed"), its ``net_flow`` (on hand plus open supply
minus qualified demand), its ``planning_zone`` ("red" at or below
the top of red, "yellow" at or below the top of yellow, "green"
at or below the top of green, "over" above), its
``order_signal`` (net flow at or below the top of yellow), its
``suggested_order_units`` (the ceiling of the top of green minus
the net flow when the signal, else 0), its
``planning_priority_pct`` (100 times the net flow over the top of
green, rounded to one decimal place, null when the top of green is
0), its ``on_hand_status`` ("stocked_out" at or below 0,
"critical" below half the top of red, "low" below the top of red,
"ok" otherwise) and its ``on_hand_pct_of_red`` (100 times the on
hand over the top of red, rounded to one decimal place, null when
the top of red is 0).  The rows are ordered by
``planning_priority_pct`` ascending (nulls last), then item_code
and site_code, and the response carries a ``summary`` of the
signal and on-hand-status counts.  Nothing is written.

The plan status of each captured buffer over the last days.

Open to any authenticated user (the router is mounted behind the
app's authentication gate).  ``days`` is 7 to 730 (default 90);
anything else answers 422.  The window is the ``days`` days ending
on the latest ``snapshot_on`` in ``ddmrp_status_snapshots`` (the
window's last day), and each row covers one item-site with at
least one snapshot row in the window: ``item_code``, ``site_code``,
its ``days_observed`` (the window days it has a snapshot row for)
and the percentage of its observed days whose ``planning_zone`` was
"red", "yellow", "green" or "over" and whose ``on_hand_status`` was
"stocked_out" or "critical", each percentage rounded to one decimal
place.  The rows are ordered by the red percentage descending, then
``item_code`` and ``site_code``.  With no snapshot row at all,
``from`` and ``to`` are null and ``rows`` is empty.  The response
is ``{"from", "to", "rows"}`` and nothing is written.

The DDMRP buffer candidates: the "A" and "B" class item-sites
without a stored designation.

Open to any authenticated user (the router is mounted behind the
app's authentication gate).  As of the demand statistics' default
as-of date (``app.stats.demand.default_as_of``) — the date
``GET /api/ddmrp/zones`` answers as of — one row per item-site of
``app.recommend.abc.abc_for_all`` whose ``abc_class`` is "A" or
"B" and which has no stored row in ``ddmrp_buffers``: the whole
ABC pool, item-sites not yet designated as decoupling points
included.  For each pool item-site the ``adu`` (the item-site's
average daily usage over the ``ddmrp.adu_window_days`` window),
the ``dlt_days`` with its ``dlt_source`` and the ``demand_class``
are the very same shared computation the zones route uses
(``_ddmrp_item_site_stats`` over one ``_ddmrp_stat_context``
read).  An item-site is a candidate only when its
``demand_class`` is not "no_demand", its ``adu`` is above 0 and
its ``dlt_days`` is at least ``MIN_CANDIDATE_DLT_DAYS`` (7: a
buffer shorter than a week of lead time rarely pays for itself).
Each row carries the pair, its ``abc_class`` and
``annual_value``, its ``demand_class``, ``adu``, ``dlt_days`` and
``dlt_source`` and a ``reason`` reading "<class> class, <whole
days>-day lead time, <demand_class> demand".  The rows are
ordered by ``annual_value`` descending, then ``item_code``, then
``site_code``.  Nothing is written.

List every stored DDMRP adjustment factor.

Open to any authenticated user (the router is mounted behind the

Nothing is written.

schema.title: Response List Ddmrp Adjustments Api Ddmrp Adjustments Get

post.description:
Store one DDMRP adjustment factor.

Admin only.  With both codes given the pair must be a row of
item_sites (a pair that is not in item_sites answers 404); with
both absent the factor applies to every stored buffer.  The
window [start_on, end_on] is inclusive and may not overlap a
stored adjustment of the same scope — the same item-site pair, or
both all-buffer (a shared boundary date overlaps) — which answers
409 with a stable machine-readable detail; the overlap check and
the store hold one transaction, serialized per scope, so a
concurrent same-scope window can never slip through the check.
The factor is a decimal strictly above 0 and at most 10; a
factor outside (0, 10], end_on before start_on, one code without
the other, an empty code or a NUL byte in any field answers 422.
The stored row records created_by as the token subject and
created_by_name its display name.  Answers 201 with the stored
row.

404.description: The item-site pair is not in item_sites.

409.description: The window overlaps a stored adjustment of the same scope.

delete.description:
Remove the stored DDMRP adjustment factor with id
``adjustment_id``.

Admin only.  Answers 204 when a stored adjustment was removed and
404 when there is no such adjustment.

get.description:
Summarise every item-site's current decision across the three kinds.

Open to any authenticated user.  The drift buckets are exactly the
buckets of ``GET /api/drift/decisions/summary`` (with the money key
named ``money``); the excess and stockout ranked rows are gathered
inside ``app.recommend.reorder.recommendations_memo``, so their
one ``recommendations_for_all`` call each (both at the request's
resolved as-of) share the memo's single computation, and an
accepted decision of those kinds is applied when its item-site is
no longer in the current ranked rows, with the money from the
stored ``money_tied_up`` / ``money_at_risk``.  ``total`` sums the
three kinds bucket by bucket, and nothing changes data.

List reorder point drift ranked by money at stake, drift rows first.

Every row carries its current planner decision (``decision``, or
null) and ``decision_lapsed``.  While ``include_decided`` is false,
a row whose current decision is a not-yet-lapsed dismissal, or a
snooze whose ``snooze_until`` is after today, is left out of the
list; with ``include_decided`` true every row is listed.  Every
row also carries ``item_description``, the item's description
from the ``inventory_items`` read model (null when the item is
not in it), from one read per request.  Rows are left out before
``offset`` and ``limit`` are applied, and every row keeps the
``rank`` that ``drift_ranked`` gave it.

schema.title: Response List Drift Api Drift Get

get.description: Export every matching drift row as a CSV attachment (no limit).

Fetch one item-site's drift row with its current planner decision.

The row is always returned with its decision and is never hidden by
a dismissal or a snooze; 404 when the item-site has no "ok"
recommendation.

post.description:
Record a planner decision for one item-site's current drift row.

The decision snapshots the current ranked drift row: its as_of, its
reorder_point_units (stored as recommended_reorder_point_units), its
current_reorder_point and its money_at_stake, with decided_by set to

404.description: No current drift row exists for the item-site.

get.description:
List stored planner decisions, newest first.

With both item_code and site_code, the full decision history of that
item-site; without either, the current decision (the latest by
decided_at, id breaking ties) of every item-site that has one.
Results are ordered by decided_at DESC, id DESC.

schema.title: Response List Planner Decisions Api Drift Decisions Get

get.description:
Summarise every item-site's current planner decision.

Open to any authenticated user.  The summary reads each
item-site's current decision (the latest by decided_at, id
breaking ties) together with the item_sites reorder points in a
fixed number of queries whatever the number of item-sites, and
answers with ``accepted``, ``applied``, ``outstanding``,
``dismissed`` and ``snoozed`` buckets.

An accepted decision is applied when the item-site's current
``item_sites.reorder_point`` is not null and differs from the
decision's ``recommended_reorder_point_units`` by at most 1; every
other accepted decision is outstanding, including one whose
item-site row is missing.  ``accepted`` therefore equals
``applied`` plus ``outstanding`` in count and in
``money_at_stake``.  ``money_at_stake`` sums the decisions'
snapshotted money at stake and ``without_money`` counts the
decisions whose snapshot is null.

Every stored budget, in month order.

Open to any signed-in user (the admin role is only needed for the
mutations); the router's include-time gate answers 401 without a
valid Bearer token.

schema.title: Response List Budgets Api Purchase Budgets Get

put.description:
Store one month's budget; needs the admin role (403 otherwise).

A new month inserts a row; an existing one updates its amount,
updated_at and updated_by — ``updated_by`` is the caller's
username — instead of creating a duplicate.  The month in the path
must be ``YYYY-MM`` with a month of 01 to 12 and the body's
``amount`` a finite number between 0 and 1,000,000,000,000
inclusive; anything else answers 422 before anything is written.
Returns the stored row.

delete.description:
Remove one month's budget; needs the admin role (403 otherwise).

204 with no body when a row was removed, 404 when the month has no
budget.

get.description:
List excess and dead stock ranked by money tied up, unknown money last.

Every row carries its current excess decision (``decision``, or
null) and ``decision_lapsed``.  While ``include_decided`` is false,
a row whose current decision is a not-yet-lapsed dismissal, or a
snooze whose ``snooze_until`` is after today (the server's UTC
date), is left out of the list; accepted, lapsed, undecided and
expired-snooze rows stay listed, and with ``include_decided`` true
every row is listed.  Every row also carries
``item_description``, the item's description from the
``inventory_items`` read model (null when the item is not in
it), from one read per request.  Rows are left out after the
``category`` and ``dead_reason`` filters and before ``offset``
and ``limit`` are applied, and every row keeps the ``rank`` that
``excess_ranked`` gave it.

While ``include_remedy`` is false (the default) the answer is
exactly that, key for key: no row carries a ``remedy`` key and
neither the ``item_sites`` levels nor the open purchase lines are
read.  While it is true and at least one row is on the page, the
``item_sites`` levels (every ``item_sites`` row) and the open
purchase lines (each ERP's newest sync) are read once each, before
any remedy is worked out; every returned row then carries
``remedy``, an ``ExcessRemedy`` proposed by the first rule that
applies — stop replenishing while units of the item are still on
order, stop replenishing while the ERP's reorder point or max
quantity is above the row's justified units (0 for a dead row, so
any level above zero — a level equal to the justified units is
not above it), dispose a dead row whose demand stopped, or reduce
an excess row — or null for a dead row that never moved and no
stop-replenishing rule caught.  A read that raises is caught and
leaves every row's ``remedy`` null, because the
stop-replenishing rules cannot be checked: the route still
answers 200 with every row it returns, and with no row on the
page neither read runs.

schema.title: Response List Excess Api Excess Get

get.description: Export every matching excess/dead row as a CSV attachment (no limit).

post.description:
Record an excess decision for one item-site's current ranked row.

The decision snapshots the item-site's current dead-and-excess
row — the row ``GET /api/excess`` lists with no filters: its as_of,
its category and dead_reason, its on_hand_units, excess_units and
money_tied_up, with decided_by set to the token subject.  An
accepted decision carries an action (stop_replenishing, reduce or
dispose); a dismissed one a non-blank reason; a snoozed one a
snooze_until after today and at most 90 days out.  Decisions are
append-only: a new row is stored on every accepted POST, earlier
decisions are never changed or deleted, and duplicate POSTs are
accepted as separate append-only duplicates.

404.description: No current excess row exists for the item-site.

get.description:
List stored excess decisions, newest first.

Open to any authenticated user.  With both item_code and site_code,
the full decision history of that item-site; without either, the
current decision (the latest by decided_at, id breaking ties) of
every item-site that has one.  Results are ordered by decided_at
DESC, id DESC.

schema.title: Response List Excess Decisions Api Excess Decisions Get

get.description:
Count the stored remedy proposals of the current accepted excess decisions.

Over the current excess decisions (the latest per item-site,
``decided_at`` with id breaking ties) whose decision is accepted:
``accepted`` is their number.  Under each remedy kind, ``proposed``
counts those decisions whose stored proposal is of that kind and
``chosen`` counts those that also chose the kind — their action is
it — and ``total`` is the sum of the three kinds.
``without_proposal`` counts the accepted decisions with no stored
proposal (every decision recorded before the proposals were
stored, among them), so ``total.proposed`` plus
``without_proposal`` equals ``accepted``.  Open to any
authenticated user; the route writes nothing.

List every stored adoption, ordered by item_code then site_code.

Open to any authenticated user (the router is mounted behind the
app's authentication gate).

schema.title: Response List Empirical Adoptions Api Empirical Adoptions Get

put.description:
Store the adoption of one item-site, or replace the stored one.

Admin only.  The pair must be a row of item_sites, validated at
the application level (a pair that is not in item_sites answers
404).  A second adoption for the same pair replaces the stored
row — its note, its adopter and the adoption time — without
adding a second row.  The stored row records adopted_by as the
token subject and adopted_by_name as its display name, exactly as
planner decisions record decided_by and decided_by_name.

404.description: The item-site is not in item_sites.

delete.description:
Withdraw the stored adoption of one item-site.

Admin only.  Answers 204 when a stored adoption was removed and
404 when the pair had none.

404.description: The pair has no stored adoption.

get.description:
Open purchase lines to expedite, ranked by stockout urgency.

Every open line with ``open_units`` above 0 that is not more than
90 days stale is checked: a line is listed when its expected
arrival (the promise, or the order date plus the supplier's mean
lead time for the ERP's default promise) is before ``as_of``
(``late``) or after the item-site's projected stockout date
(``after_stockout``). ``as_of`` defaults to the server's current
date; one after today answers 422.

The reporting currency, and the currencies the sources report in.

``reporting_currency`` is the ``erp.reporting_currency`` system
setting, resolved exactly as ``GET /api/exceptions`` resolves it
(the stored value when it is one of the allowed currencies,
ignoring case, else the registry default), and ``sources`` one
entry per stored row of ``erp_source_currencies`` —
``source_system``, ``currency_code`` and ``seen_at`` (ISO-8601) —
ordered by source system then code, empty while no row is stored.
One read of the stored rows and one read of the stored system
settings — no writes — feed the answer; a stored row whose fields
are not strings or whose ``seen_at`` is not a timestamp
contributes nothing — nothing here can raise on a hostile row
(never a 500).

Every stored mapping, ordered by kind then source code.

``kind`` (item, site or vendor) and ``target_system`` (odoo) narrow
the result when given; a value outside the allowed ones answers 422
with the same rules as the PUT body, not an empty result.

schema.title: Response List Mappings Api Erp Mappings Get

put.description:
Store one mapping; needs the admin role (403 otherwise).

A new (kind, target_system, source_code) inserts a row; an existing
one updates its target code and updated_at instead of creating a
duplicate.  Returns the stored row.

get.description:
The suggested item mappings, read-only, for any signed-in user.

A code held in ``item_sites`` under both ``acumatica`` and ``odoo``
at different sites suggests itself (``matched_on`` ``code``); a
code in ``inventory_items`` under ``acumatica`` and a different
code there under ``odoo`` whose descriptions are equal after
trimming and ignoring case suggest the pair (``matched_on``
``description``).  A null, empty or only-spaces description never
matches — no similarity score, no partial match, no unit of
measure.  One code whose description matched several on the other
side answers one suggestion per pair, each ``ambiguous`` true.  A
code already mapped — a stored item mapping to ``odoo`` as its
``source_code``, or any mapping's ``target_code`` — is left out.
The answer is ordered by ``matched_on`` with ``code`` first, then
``source_code``, then ``target_code``; ``limit`` (1 to 1000,
default 200) caps it, and out of range answers 422.  The route
writes nothing.

schema.title: Response Suggest Mappings Api Erp Mappings Suggestions Get

delete.description:
Remove one mapping by id; needs the admin role (403 otherwise).

204 with no body when a row was removed, 404 when no mapping has
the id.

get.description:
The source systems that store item-sites, and the item-sites.

``sources`` lists each source system (a code or null) with the
number of item-sites it stores and the newest ``synced_at`` of its
rows, ordered by the count descending, then source system with null
last; ``item_sites`` lists every row as (item_code, site_code,
source_system), ordered by item_code then site_code.  One read of
``item_sites`` — one SQL statement, no writes — feeds both; with no
item-sites, both lists are empty.

Every stored grant, in force and revoked, newest first.

Open to any signed-in user (the admin role is only needed for the
mutations); the router's include-time gate answers 401 without a
valid Bearer token.

schema.title: Response List Grants Api Standing Grants Get

post.description:
Store one standing grant; needs the admin role (403 otherwise).

The body's ``process`` (one of the two release names), its finite
values above 0 (at most 1,000,000,000,000, the daily one not
below the per-document one) and its whole ``max_data_age_hours``
(1 to 168) must validate, or the body answers 422 before anything
is written.  ``created_by`` is the caller's username.  When a
grant for the process is already in force the unique index refuses
the insert — even against a racing create — and the route answers
409 with nothing written.  Returns the stored row.

get.description:
The stored standing-grant runs, newest first, at most ``limit``.

Open to any signed-in user, like the grants list; the router's
include-time gate answers 401 without a valid Bearer token.
``limit`` is an integer from 1 to 200, default 50, and
``process`` one of the two release names, narrowing the answer to
that process's runs when given; anything else answers 422 in
FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope, never a 500.  Each run is
the stored row: ``id``, ``process`` and ``grant_id``,
``started_at`` with its UTC offset, ``outcome`` and ``reason``
(null when the run has none), ``documents`` and ``value`` and
``left_out`` in their stored order.  The route never writes.

schema.title: Response List Grant Runs Api Standing Grants Runs Get

post.description:
Revoke one grant by id; needs the admin role (403 otherwise).

``revoked_at`` is set to now and ``revoked_by`` to the caller's
username, answered with the revoked row.  ``id`` is an integer
from 1 to 9223372036854775807, the largest the bigint column
holds; anything else answers 422.  404 when no row has that id,
409 when the row is already revoked.

get.description:
The exceptions triage list of the fifteen sources.

Open to any signed-in user (the router is mounted behind the
app's authentication gate).  Each source is read once per call;
a source that raises is caught and listed in ``sources_failed``
while the other sources still answer (status 200).  The rows are
ordered high before medium, then kind order, then item_code and
key; ``as_of`` is the latest as-of date reported by any
successful source (null when none reports one).

The order minimums source reads the stored supplier order
minimums once per call and, only when at least one is stored,
builds the 7-day order plan (the horizon ``GET /api/supply-plan``
and the Order plan screen default to), through
``build_supply_plan``: one row per plan supplier group that
carries a minimum and a shortfall above 0 and holds a line whose
``due_in_days`` is at most the
``exceptions.order_minimum_due_days`` system setting (default
2), kind "order_below_minimum", severity "high" when one of the
group's lines has a ``due_in_days`` of 0, else "medium", the key
"order_below_minimum:<source_system>:<supplier_code>",
``item_code`` and ``site_code`` null, title "Order below
supplier minimum", the detail "The order to <name> comes to
<total_value>, <shortfall> below its minimum of <minimum>;
<item_code> at <site_code> must be ordered by <order_by>."
(the name the group's name, else its supplier code; the line
named the group's first; the amounts dollars and cents with
thousands separators, ``order_by`` read ``YYYY-MM-DD``), view
"#/orders" and ``detected_on`` the plan's ``as_of`` (the plan's
``as_of`` is the rows' ``detected_on`` only, never the
response's ``as_of``; a failure of the minimums read or of the
plan build fails the source, listed "order_minimums").

The standing grants source reads the grants in force, once per
call for each of ``order_plan_release`` and
``transfer_release``, and each process's latest standing-grant
run: with the ``erp.standing_grants_enabled`` switch from the
stored system settings stored false (a missing value, or one
that is not a boolean, counts as on) it raises nothing; a
latest run under the grant in force that failed, that skipped,
or that released with a ``left_out`` that is not empty is one
row, and a grant whose time (the later of its ``created_at``
and the latest run's ``started_at`` under the grant, or
``created_at`` alone while the process has no run under the
grant) is more than ``STANDING_GRANT_IDLE_HOURS`` (26 — one
daily sync plus two hours) hours before the current UTC time is
one idle row, whatever the latest run's outcome: kind
"standing_grant_run", severity "high" for a failed run and for
the idle row, else "medium", ``item_code`` and ``site_code``
null, title "Standing grant run needs attention", view
"#/releases", the key "standing_grant_run:<run id>" (the idle
row's key "standing_grant_run:idle:<grant id>:<the latest run
id under the grant, or 0>") and ``detected_on`` the run's UTC
date (the idle row's the grant's time plus 26 hours) — neither
ever the response's ``as_of``; a failure of the grants read or
of the runs read fails the source, listed
"standing_grants".

Every row carries the stored acknowledgement of its key, when
there is one: ``acknowledged`` (true) plus
``acknowledged_by_name``, ``acknowledged_at`` and
``snooze_until`` — all null or false while the key is
unacknowledged.  A row snoozed until a date after the as-of date
is left out of the rows and the counts unless the request passes
``include_snoozed=true``, and acknowledgements whose key no
longer appears in the list are simply ignored.  ``counts`` count
only the rows returned and carry ``acknowledged``.  Nothing is
written and no ERP client is called.

Every row also carries its first-seen date from the
``exception_first_seen`` table, read once per call and never
written: ``first_seen_on`` (the date the key was first captured,
or null when it has never been captured) and ``new`` (true only
when ``first_seen_on`` equals the response's as-of date), and
``counts`` carries ``new``, the number of returned rows whose
``new`` is true.  A failure reading the table is caught: every
row then reads ``first_seen_on`` null and ``new`` false, and the
route still answers 200.

put.description:
Store or replace the acknowledgement of one current exception.

Admin only — the same ``require_role("admin")`` the planner
decisions use: a non-admin write answers 403 and no token 401.
The body carries the exception's stable key plus the optional
snooze and note; an empty key, a NUL byte or a key that would not
fit the stored column answers 422, a ``snooze_until`` in the past
(against the current UTC date at request time, never the response
as-of date) answers 422, and a key that is not in the current
exceptions list answers 404.  ``acknowledged_by`` is the token
subject and ``acknowledged_by_name`` its display name.  The
response is the stored row: a second PUT of the key replaces the
row — the new subject and name, a fresh ``acknowledged_at``, and
the request's snooze and note (an omitted ``snooze_until`` or
``note`` clears the stored value).

404.description: The key is not in the current exceptions list.

delete.description:
Remove the acknowledgement stored for one key.

Admin only — the same ``require_role("admin")`` the planner
decisions use: a non-admin write answers 403 and no token 401.
Answers 204 when the key's acknowledgement is removed and 404
when no acknowledgement is stored for the key — a key that is no
longer in the exceptions list keeps its acknowledgement until it
is removed.

404.description: No acknowledgement is stored for the key.

get.description: Freshness of the five OData feed tables (read-only, no admin gate).

The current guidance, for any signed-in user (401 without a token).

Read-only: the route writes nothing.  ``publication`` is null
and ``items`` empty when nothing was ever published; otherwise
``publication`` is the newest row of ``guidance_publications``
(``id``, ``source``, ``published_at`` as an ISO-8601 string with
a UTC offset, ``published_by`` and ``item_count``) and
``items`` the versions whose ``last_publication_id`` is that
id — each with ``key``, ``hash``, ``stamp`` (the key, ``@`` and
the hash), ``type``, ``scope``, ``area``, ``area_title``,
``title``, ``statement``, ``status``, ``decided_by``,
``decided_on`` (a ``YYYY-MM-DD`` string), ``decided_under``,
``decided_ref`` and ``authority`` (each a string or null) and
``since`` (the ``published_at`` of the publication the row's
``first_publication_id`` names: the moment AIERP first held this
version).  The route sorts the versions itself: by type in the
order direction, boundary, roadmap, design; within a type by the
number at the end of the key, compared as a number and
ascending; and for the same number by the key in Unicode code
point order — so the order never depends on the database's
collation.  The fixed field set is serialized with explicit
null values and no extra field.

put.description:
Publish the whole guidance; needs the admin role (403 otherwise).

The admin check (401 without a valid token, 403 for a signed-in
non-admin) and the raw-body storeability guard are declared
before the body on purpose: both run before the body model is
validated, so the 401/403 come before any validation and a raw
body the 422 envelope could not echo back is refused by the
guard first.

``source`` and every item must validate or the body answers 422
before anything is written (one wrong item refuses the whole
publication).  When every item matches the current version of its
key and every current key is in the body, nothing is written;
otherwise one new ``guidance_publications`` row (``source`` as
sent, ``published_by`` the caller's username, ``item_count`` the
number of items) and, per item, a bump of the matching current
row's ``last_publication_id`` or a new ``guidance_versions`` row —
all in one database transaction.  Returns ``changed``,
``publication_id`` (the id of the newest publication after the
call), ``items``, ``new_versions`` and ``withdrawn``.

get.description:
The history of one item, for any signed-in user (401 without a token).

Read-only: the route writes nothing.  The key in the path must
match ``^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,7}-[NRDB]-[0-9]{1,4}$`` or the request
answers 422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope; a key no
row of ``guidance_versions`` has answers 404.  Otherwise the
answer is ``key``, ``current`` (true when one of the item's
versions is current — its ``last_publication_id`` is the id of
the newest publication) and ``versions``: every row with that
key, the newest first (by row ``id``, descending), each with its
fixed field set, its ``current`` flag and its ``first``/``last``
publication (``publication_id``, ``source``, ``published_at`` as
an ISO-8601 string with a UTC offset and ``published_by``).
Every signed-in user, admin or not, gets the same answer.

What one stamp names, for any signed-in user (401 without a token).

Read-only: the route writes nothing.  The stamp in the path is a
key, the character ``@`` and 10 characters from ``0`` to ``9``
and ``a`` to ``f``; anything else answers 422 in FastAPI's
HTTPValidationError envelope.  A stamp no row has answers 404 —
also when the key exists with other hashes.  Otherwise the answer
is ``stamp``, ``key`` and ``hash`` (the stamp's parts), the
``type``, ``title`` and ``statement`` those rows carry (the words
the stamp names), ``current`` (true when a row with that key and
hash is current), ``superseded`` (true when the key has a current
row with another hash) and ``versions``: every row with that key
and that hash, the newest first (by row ``id``, descending).
Every signed-in user, admin or not, gets the same answer.

List one row per item-site that has a forecast, for any signed-in user.

Ordered by ``total_forecast`` descending, then ``item_code`` and
``site_code``; item-sites whose demand class is ``no_demand`` are
left out. ``demand_class`` filters the list, ``as_of`` sets the date
(the shared ``app.stats.demand`` default when absent), and
``limit`` / ``offset`` page it.

schema.title: Response List Forecasts Api Forecast Get

get.description:
One item-site's forecast row plus the ``history`` it was built from.

Answers 404 when the item-site has no demand events, or when its
demand class is ``no_demand``.

post.description:
Capture (or fetch) the forecast snapshot for one as-of date.

Admin only. The JSON body is optional and may carry ``as_of`` (a
date); without it the shared default as-of date is captured with
origin ``live``, and an ``as_of`` given stores origin
``backfill``. When the date already has a snapshot nothing is
stored and the stored snapshot's fields come back with ``created``
false. A date later than today, or a malformed one, answers 422
in FastAPI's validation envelope.

get.description:
List the stored forecast snapshots, newest as-of date first.

Any signed-in user. Each entry carries the snapshot-level fields
``as_of``, ``origin``, ``item_sites``, ``rows`` and
``created_at``; ``limit`` (default 50, 1 to 500) and ``offset``
page the list.

schema.title: Response List Forecast Snapshots Api Forecast Snapshots Get

get.description:
The realised accuracy of the stored forecast snapshots, any signed-in user.

Each completed snapshot bucket (``bucket_end`` on or before
``as_of`` — the shared default as-of date when absent, because
demand after the latest demand date is unknown, not zero) is
compared with the actual demand of its range.  ``origin``
(``live`` or ``backfill``) keeps only snapshots of that origin
and ``bucket_index`` (1 to 12) only that horizon.  ``limit``
(default 100, 1 to 1000) and ``offset`` page ``item_sites`` only;
``overall`` and ``by_horizon`` always cover everything compared.
A malformed ``as_of``, ``origin`` or ``bucket_index`` answers 422
in FastAPI's validation envelope.

The realised value of the stored demand signals, any signed-in user.

Only completed snapshot buckets with a stored
``signal_quantity`` above 0 (``bucket_end`` on or before
``as_of`` — the shared default as-of date when absent, because
demand after the latest demand date is unknown, not zero) are
compared with the actual demand of their range; a bucket whose
signal is null or 0 is left out.  ``origin`` (``live`` or
``backfill``) keeps only snapshots of that origin.  ``item_sites``
is ordered by ``signal_total`` descending, then ``item_code``
and ``site_code``.  A malformed ``as_of`` or ``origin`` answers
422 in FastAPI's validation envelope.

post.description:
Store a planner override for one forecast period (admin only).

through ``OdooClient.preview_draft_purchase_order`` (read-only:
only ``search_read`` reads, never a create, and no consultation of
``ODOO_ALLOW_WRITES``) and answers ``200`` with ``dry_run`` true,
``would_create``, the origin tag, the resolved ids, and ``existing``
— the draft order already carrying the origin, or null. The dry
run is open to any signed-in user.

With ``confirm`` true the admin role is required: a signed-in
non-admin is refused with 403 before any Odoo call and no audit
row is written.  Otherwise the route calls
``OdooClient.create_draft_purchase_order`` under the per-
``(target item code, target site code)`` lock and, on its own
connection, the per-``(target item code, target site code)``
PostgreSQL advisory lock (so the serialization holds across API
worker processes) and answers ``200`` with ``dry_run`` false and
the client's ``{odoo_id, name, state, already_existed}``.  A
confirm that cannot take the advisory lock within the timeout
answers 409 with the fixed "Another draft order for this item-site
is in progress" — the Odoo create is never called and no audit row
is written.  After the Odoo call settles the route appends one row
to the append-only ``draft_po_actions`` audit (the actor, the
request's fields, the translated target codes, and the outcome —
``created`` or ``already_existed`` with the Odoo id and name, or
``error`` with the exception class); if that insert fails the
request answers 500.  The origin is never caller-supplied: it is
always the client's system-generated item-site default, computed
from the translated codes, so two source codes mapped to the same
Odoo item-site share one open draft.

cannot take the per-item-site advisory lock in time is a 409 with
the fixed "Another draft order for this item-site is in progress"
message; a disabled write switch on a confirm is a 409 with the
fixed "Odoo writes are disabled" message; a resolution failure or any other Odoo error is
a 502 naming which resolution failed — and, for a resolution
failure, the code the client was called with and whether it was
mapped — or a generic upstream message; a client ``ValueError`` is
a 422.

get.description:
Second-source candidates for the sole-source items.

Open to any signed-in user behind the app's auth gate (401
without a valid Bearer token).  ``second_sources`` reads the
supplier risk rating once, the stored
``second_source.similar_prefix_length`` once, every supplier
terms row once, every inventory item once and every supplier
once, and writes nothing and calls no ERP.  One entry per item
code of each risk entry's ``sole_source_item_codes``
(``supplier_code``, ``supplier_name``, ``late``, ``variable`` and
``supplier_risk`` from the risk entry, ``description`` the item's
inventory item description, null when it has none), and one
candidate per other supplier with a terms row for the item: when
one supplier holds several rows, the candidate is the row marked
``is_default``, then the one with the shortest ``lead_time_
days``, then the lowest ``source_system``; a terms candidate
carries ``supplier_name`` — the name in the suppliers table, else
the risk entry's ``supplier_name``, else null — ``source_
system``, ``lead_time_days`` and ``min_order_qty`` from the
chosen row, ``risk`` that supplier's risk entry's ``risk``, null
when the rating has no entry for it, ``basis`` ``terms`` and
``similar_items`` null.  They are followed by at most three
similar candidates — suppliers with a terms row for a different
item whose code starts with the same first N characters as the
entry's item code, N the whole-number part of the stored
``second_source.similar_prefix_length`` (the registry default
when nothing is stored; 0 turns similar suggestions off), the
entry's own supplier and the entry's terms candidates never among
them — carrying ``supplier_name`` found the same way, ``risk``
null when unrated, ``basis`` ``similar``, ``similar_items`` the
number of distinct such item codes, and null ``source_system``,
``lead_time_days`` and ``min_order_qty``, ranked ``risk``
``low``, then ``medium``, then ``high``, then null, then
``similar_items`` descending, then ``supplier_code``.  Entries
are ordered ``supplier_risk`` ``high``, then ``medium``, then
``low``, then ``item_code``, then ``supplier_code``.

Every entry also carries its bridge stock: ``daily_demand`` the
sum of the ``inputs.d`` of ``recommendations_for_all``'s rows of
the item whose ``inputs.d`` is a number, rounded to 2 places,
null when there is no such row; ``bridge_days`` the
``lead_time_days`` of the first terms candidate with a lead time
above 0 (a lead time of 0 means the ERP holds none and never
counts), ``bridge_basis`` ``candidate_lead_time``, else — while
the entry has a terms candidate at all — the largest
``inputs.lt`` of ``recommendations_for_all``'s rows of the item
that is a number above 0, rounded up to a whole number of days,
``bridge_basis`` ``item_lead_time``, else the stored
``second_source.qualification_days`` (the registry default when
nothing is stored), ``bridge_basis`` ``qualification_days``;
``bridge_units`` ``daily_demand`` times ``bridge_days``, rounded
up to a whole number; ``on_hand_units`` the sum of those rows'
``on_hand_units``, 0 when there is none; ``bridge_short_units``
``bridge_units`` minus ``on_hand_units``, never below 0; and
``bridge_arithmetic`` the sentence ``<daily_demand> a day x
<bridge_days> days = <bridge_units> units; on hand
<on_hand_units>, short <bridge_short_units>`` — the bridge
fields null, ``on_hand_units`` null too, when the recommendations
read raised.

The safety-stock cost curve of the service levels, per ABC class.

The ``app.recommend.service_curve.service_level_curve`` answer,
built from one ``recommendations_for_all`` read (no as-of) and one
stored system settings read: for each ABC class, one point per
ladder level (0.90, 0.92, 0.95, 0.97, 0.98, 0.99 and 0.995 plus
the class' current level when that is not already one of them)
with the safety stock in units and in money, its yearly holding
cost and the difference to the previous point's, and the expected
fill rate at the level (null when no item-site of the class takes
part in it); the class' ``fill_rate_item_sites`` counts the
taking-part item-sites.

The cheapest combination of per-class service levels reaching a
target expected fill rate.

Built from one ``recommendations_for_all`` read (no as-of) and
one stored system settings read — the same reads the curve takes,
once — it answers ``as_of``, ``service_target`` and
``holding_rate`` as the curve reports them, ``current`` (the
combination of the classes' current levels) and ``highest`` (each
class' highest ladder level), and ``suggested``: the combination
with the lowest holding cost among those whose expected fill rate
is at least ``target_fill_rate``, a tie going to the lower level
for A, then for B, then for C (null when no combination reaches
the target or no row takes part), with
``holding_cost_delta`` the difference to the current holding
cost.  A combination is one ladder level for each of the classes
``A``, ``B`` and ``C``; its sums are worked out once per class
and ladder level, so no row is solved again for each of the
combinations.

row, and the switched line's ``supplier_reason`` naming the
default pick's supplier, its risk and its signs.

The top-ups of the order plan (1 to 60 horizon days, default 7),
for any signed-in user.

The supplier groups of the ``horizon_days`` order plan that have a
stored minimum and a shortfall above 0 — the groups
``GET /api/supply-plan`` reports with its ``minimum`` and
``shortfall``, in the plan's group order — each answered with the
lines of the order plan built for
``supply_plan.top_up_lookahead_days`` (the stored value rounded
down to a whole number of days, else the default) at the same
as-of that can top the group up: the group's same
``supplier_code`` and ``source_system`` lines whose
``due_in_days`` is above the horizon, whose ``value`` is not null
and whose (``item_code``, ``site_code``) is not on the excess list
(``excess_ranked`` read once per call).  The candidates are taken
by ``due_in_days``, then ``item_code``, then ``site_code``, each
added until the sum of the values taken is at least the shortfall —
the candidate that reaches it included, none after it — each a
top-up with the look-ahead line's ``item_code``, ``site_code``,
``due_in_days``, ``order_by``, ``quantity``, ``unit_cost`` and
``value`` plus ``holding_cost`` (the value × the effective
``replenishment.holding_rate`` the recommendations use ×
``due_in_days`` / 365, rounded to two places half up).
``top_up_value`` is the top-ups' values summed (0 with none),
``reaches_minimum`` true when ``total_value`` plus
``top_up_value`` is at least the stored minimum and ``still_short``
the minimum minus the two when that is above 0, else 0.  Read-only.

The inter-site transfer suggestions, for any signed-in user.

Per item-site (the recommendation with status "ok" and a numeric
recommended order quantity): the position — on hand plus on order —
against the reorder point and the order quantity, a need when the
reorder point stands above the position, a surplus when the
position stands above the reorder point plus one order quantity.
Per item, across the item-sites of the same source system, the
largest need is served first, from the largest surplus first — each
match the smaller of the two remainders in whole units, both
reduced by it, a site never giving to itself.  The suggestions are
ordered by value descending (the ones without a value last), then
item_code.

The one-page summary of the 7-day supply plan, for any
signed-in user.

``line_count``, ``total_value`` and ``supplier_count`` are the
7-day order plan's ``line_count``, ``total_value`` and the
number of its supplier groups with a non-null
``supplier_code`` — the plan ``GET
/api/supply-plan?horizon_days=7`` answers, built by the same
``build_supply_plan`` call — and ``transfer_count`` and
``transfer_value`` are the transfer suggestions'
``suggestion_count`` and ``total_value``, the suggestions
``GET /api/supply-plan/transfers`` answers, built by the same
``build_transfer_suggestions`` call.  The two builders run
inside one ``recommendations_memo``: the first reads its
``recommendations_for_all`` through the memo and the second
answers from it, so the recommendations are computed exactly
once per request.  ``transfers_in_flight`` counts the rows
``TransferReleasePostgresRepository.list_in_flight`` returns
whose ``erp_status`` is null or none of "Released", "Completed"
and "Canceled", and ``transfers_awaiting_release`` how many of
those are at least the
``exceptions.release_approval_days`` system setting (default 3)
old by ``updated_at`` — a missing or out-of-range stored value
falls back to the registry default, the exact cutoff inclusive,
as the exceptions inbox' transfer window is.

post.description:
Preview or confirm the release of the due supply-plan lines.

The plan is ``app.supply.release.order_plan_release(horizon_days,
supplier_codes, top_ups)`` — the lines the ``GET /api/supply-plan``
builder produces for ``horizon_days``, kept for the named
suppliers, one group per (site, supplier) of the ``acumatica``
lines with its origin tag "AIERP order plan <as_of> site
<site_code> vendor <supplier_code>" (the as-of is the builder's
resolved as-of, never regenerated at confirm time) — and the
body's ``top_ups`` are passed through to it: each named top-up the
``GET /api/supply-plan/top-ups`` suggestions hold at the release's
as-of joins its (site, supplier) group as a line — the group
created, with the same origin tag a due line's group would carry,
when the supplier has no due line at that site — and a named
top-up the suggestions do not hold adds nothing and is listed in
``unreleasable`` as "not a suggested top-up".  The answer is the
shared ``release_groups`` body of ``app.api.aggregate``: a preview
(``confirm`` false or absent, any signed-in user) with the
Acumatica outcome of each group on top, and a confirm (admin only
— 403 otherwise — the advisory lock, 409 on a second confirm, 503
on incomplete Acumatica configuration, 409 on switched-off writes,
one ``plan_releases`` row per group with its outcome, a 502 marking
the rows aborted) exactly as ``POST /api/aggregate/release`` does
it.  A named supplier's lines from another source system come back
as ``unreleasable``; a code no line of the plan carries is simply
absent — 200 with the groups the named suppliers hold, never a
422.

Preview or confirm the release of the chosen transfer suggestions.

The plan is
``app.supply.transfer_release.transfer_release_plan`` over the
current suggestions — the suggestions the
``GET /api/supply-plan/transfers`` builder produces, read once,
each requested entry matched by (item_code, from_site, to_site)
with the suggestion's quantity, one group per (from_site,
to_site) with the origin tag "AIERP transfer <as_of> site
<from_site> to <to_site>" (in the preview the as-of is the
builder's resolved as-of; in the confirm it is the snapshot
resolved after the release's advisory lock is taken, so the audit
row records the same snapshot the release used) — the unmatched
entries as ``unreleasable`` ("no longer suggested") and the
non-Acumatica suggestions ("only Acumatica transfers are released
here").

A preview (``confirm`` false or absent, any signed-in user) calls
the client's transfer preview once with every group and answers
the plan with each group's outcome, reference number and warehouse
codes on top — all null with an incomplete Acumatica
configuration, no client call — writing nothing.

A confirm (``confirm`` true) is admin only (403 otherwise, before
any ERP call or row) and holds the transfer release's advisory
lock — a second confirm waits, 409 when it cannot take it — then
resolves the as-of snapshot, builds the plan and, before any
row: incomplete Acumatica configuration 503, switched-off writes
409.  Otherwise one ``pending`` ``transfer_releases`` row per
group is written (the caller's username and display name as the
actor), and the client's transfer create is called once with
every group — the orders are created ON HOLD, moving the stock
still requires releasing the hold under Acumatica's own process —
and
each row is updated to the group's outcome (``created`` or
``exists``) with its reference number, warehouse codes and error,
returning the plan with each group's outcome.  An ``exists``
outcome carries the existing order's reference number only when
the current plan's lines match every stored snapshot of the same
origin — a changed plan keeps the outcome but not the reference
number, with the stale-lines error in the row and the answer, and
the confirm still answers 200, never a 409.  An Acumatica auth or
transport failure that aborts the batch is 502 and marks the
release's rows ``aborted``, so the audit always shows every
release attempt.  A confirm with no releasable groups is 200
with empty groups and calls Acumatica not at all.

get.description:
The newest stored transfer release rows, at most ``limit`` of
them (1 to 200, default 50); admin only.

ADMIN-ONLY, checked via ``require_admin`` exactly like the confirm:
a signed-in non-admin is refused with 403 and without a token with
401, before any row is read.
