AbcCounts.title: AbcCounts
AbcCounts.description: How many item-sites landed in each class (and how many did not).

AbcResponse.title: AbcResponse
AbcResponse.description:
The ABC classification of the item-sites as of ``as_of``.

``as_of`` is the query value when one was given, else the shared
default as-of date (``app.stats.demand.default_as_of``); it is
never null. ``total_annual_value`` is the sum of the classified
item-sites' annual values (0.0 when there are none), ``counts``
the :class:`AbcCounts` of the rows and ``rows`` the
``app.recommend.abc.abc_for_all`` output.

AbcRow.title: AbcRow
AbcRow.description:
One item-site's ABC row (an ``app.recommend.abc.classify`` row).

``annual_value`` is a year of the item-site's daily demand at its
unit cost (``365 * d * unit_cost`` of its ``"ok"`` recommendation)
and null when the item-site is unclassified; ``rank`` is 1-based
among the classified item-sites (null when unclassified),
``share_before`` the cumulative share of the annual values ranked
before the item-site (null when unclassified) and ``abc_class``
the ``"A"`` / ``"B"`` / ``"C"`` class (null when unclassified).

AccuracyHorizon.title: AccuracyHorizon
AccuracyHorizon.description: The measures for one horizon (``bucket_index``) plus its count.

AccuracyItemSite.title: AccuracyItemSite
AccuracyItemSite.description: One item-site's measures, with its most recent compared method.

AccuracyMeasures.title: AccuracyMeasures
AccuracyMeasures.description:
The measures over one set of compared snapshot buckets.

``forecast_total``, ``wape`` and ``bias`` stay the statistical
forecast's [rule: OVR-4]; ``effective_total``, ``effective_wape``
and ``effective_bias`` are the same with each bucket's effective
quantity — a null stored ``effective_quantity`` reads as its
``quantity`` and as not overridden, and the stored
``signal_quantity`` (a null one reads as 0) stays in it — in
place of the statistical one, ``overridden_buckets`` how many
compared buckets had at least one overridden day, and
``value_added`` ``wape`` minus the error of the effective
forecast before the signals — each bucket's effective quantity
minus its signal quantity — over the actuals (null when
``actual_total`` is 0), positive when the overrides, measured
alone, moved the forecast nearer the actuals.

AccuracyResult.title: AccuracyResult
AccuracyResult.description:
The realised accuracy of the stored forecast snapshots.

``overall`` covers everything compared, ``by_horizon`` carries one
entry per ``bucket_index`` present, in order, and ``item_sites``
one entry per item-site (the ``method`` from its most recent
compared snapshot), ordered by ``actual_total`` descending, then
``item_code`` and ``site_code``.  A snapshot bucket is compared
only when its ``bucket_end`` is on or before ``as_of``; with no
``as_of`` the shared default as-of date is used, so demand after
the latest demand date is unknown, not zero.

AckBody.title: AckBody
AckBody.description:
The acknowledgement request: the exception's stable key plus
the optional snooze date and note (null when omitted, which
clears the stored value).

AckRow.title: AckRow
AckRow.description: The stored acknowledgement row, as answered by the PUT.

AuthConfigResponse.title: AuthConfigResponse
AuthConfigResponse.description:
The public authentication configuration served to the frontend.

Exactly these fields — never ``AUTH_DEV_TOKEN``, ``AUTH_DEV_ROLES``
or any other secret, in any mode.

raw_claims.title: Raw Claims
raw_claims.description: Full token claims for future extension

AuthUser.title: AuthUser
AuthUser.description: Represents the currently authenticated user derived from token claims.

ChangeContributions.title: ChangeContributions
ChangeContributions.description: Shapley contribution of each input to the reorder-point change.

ChangeInputs.title: ChangeInputs
ChangeInputs.description: The demand and lead-time inputs behind one recommendation.

CrossErpItemsResponse.title: CrossErpItemsResponse
CrossErpItemsResponse.description:
The cross-ERP item comparison answer.

``as_of`` is the shared default as-of date; ``rows`` is one entry
per stored mapping of kind ``item``, ordered by ``source_code``
(empty — still a 200 — while no mapping is stored).

CrossErpRow.title: CrossErpRow
CrossErpRow.description:
One stored item mapping compared side by side.

``description`` is the ``inventory_items`` description of either
code (the source's first, else null).  ``sides`` is exactly two
entries — the source code's item-sites first, then the target
code's item-sites under ``odoo``.  ``opportunity`` is true when
one side has a site whose ``stockout_category`` is not null and
the other side has a site whose ``excess_units`` is above 0;
``short_side`` and ``excess_side`` then read that side's index in
``sides`` and ``suggested_move_units`` is the smaller of the
need, the short side's non-null-stockout sites summed over their
gap — the site's ``reorder_point_units`` minus its
``on_hand_units``, never below 0, a site with a null reorder
point counting 0 — and the excess side's sites summed over their
``excess_units``, rounded down to a whole number and never below
0.  Otherwise ``opportunity`` is false and all three are null.

CrossErpSide.title: CrossErpSide
CrossErpSide.description:
One side of the comparison: one code's item-sites.

``source_system`` is the source of that side's item-sites (null
when the side has none), ``sites`` the side's site entries ordered
by ``site_code`` and ``on_hand_units`` the sum over the sites (0
with no sites).

CrossErpSite.title: CrossErpSite
CrossErpSite.description:
One item-site's figures on one side of the comparison.

``on_hand_units`` is the stored on hand (0 when there is no
on-hand row).  ``daily_demand`` is the item-site's
recommendation's ``inputs.d``, ``days_of_cover`` the on hand over
the demand rounded to one decimal (null when the demand is 0 or
null), and ``status``, ``reorder_point_units`` and
``suggested_order_quantity`` the recommendation's own fields —
each null when the item-site has no recommendation.
``stockout_category`` is the item-site's ``stockout_ranked``
category (null when it has no row there) and ``excess_units`` its
``excess_ranked`` excess units (0 when it has no row there).

CurrentSettings.title: CurrentSettings
CurrentSettings.description: The item-site's current planning settings from item_sites.

DdmrpAdjustment.title: DdmrpAdjustment
DdmrpAdjustment.description:
One stored DDMRP adjustment factor.

``item_code`` and ``site_code`` are both null for an adjustment
that applies to every stored buffer, and both set for one of
them.  ``factor`` (a decimal strictly above 0 and at most 10)
scales the average daily usage between ``start_on`` and ``end_on``
(inclusive).

factor.title: Factor
factor.description: The adjustment factor, a decimal number strictly greater than 0 and at most 10.

DdmrpAdjustmentBody.title: DdmrpAdjustmentBody
DdmrpAdjustmentBody.description:
The body of POST /api/ddmrp/adjustments.

``item_code`` and ``site_code`` are both absent (an adjustment
for every stored buffer) or both given (one item-site).  Every
business rule is a model validation, so a rejected body answers
422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope, exactly like a
malformed one.

DdmrpBuffer.title: DdmrpBuffer
DdmrpBuffer.description: One stored DDMRP buffer designation for an item-site.

DdmrpBufferBody.title: DdmrpBufferBody
DdmrpBufferBody.description:
The body of PUT /api/ddmrp/buffers.

Every business rule is a model validation, so a rejected body
answers 422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope, exactly like
a malformed one.

DdmrpCandidateResponse.title: DdmrpCandidateResponse
DdmrpCandidateResponse.description:
The DDMRP buffer candidates, as of one date.

The rows are ordered by ``annual_value`` descending, then
``item_code``, then ``site_code``.

DdmrpCandidateRow.title: DdmrpCandidateRow
DdmrpCandidateRow.description:
One DDMRP buffer candidate item-site.

An "A" or "B" class item-site of the as-of ABC pool that has no
stored row in ``ddmrp_buffers``.  ``demand_class`` is null when
the pair has no demand statistics, and ``dlt_days`` with its
``dlt_source`` are null when neither lead time source exists —
the same nullability as the zones route's shared statistics,
which the qualification rules keep out of the answered rows.

DdmrpPerformanceResponse.title: DdmrpPerformanceResponse
DdmrpPerformanceResponse.description:
The DDMRP plan status of every captured buffer, over one window.

``from`` and ``to`` bound the window of ``days`` days ending on the
latest ``snapshot_on`` (both null when no snapshot row exists), and
``rows`` carries one row per item-site with a snapshot in the
window, ordered by the red share descending, then item_code and
site_code.

DdmrpPerformanceRow.title: DdmrpPerformanceRow
DdmrpPerformanceRow.description:
One item-site's observed plan status over the window.

``days_observed`` is the number of the window's days the pair has a
``ddmrp_status_snapshots`` row for, and the percentages are the
shares of those observed days in each planning zone (``red_pct``,
``yellow_pct``, ``green_pct``, ``over_pct``) and on-hand status
(``stocked_out_pct``, ``critical_pct``), each rounded to one
decimal place.

DdmrpPlanResponseWithAdjustment.title: DdmrpPlanResponseWithAdjustment
DdmrpPlanResponseWithAdjustment.description: The DDMRP plan, with the adjustment-factor fields on every row.

DdmrpPlanRowWithAdjustment.title: DdmrpPlanRowWithAdjustment
DdmrpPlanRowWithAdjustment.description:
A plan row that keeps the adjustment-factor fields of the
shared zone row: ``adu_base`` (the unadjusted ADU) and
``adjustment_factor`` (the active factor applied to it), so the
plan route returns them without omission.

DdmrpPlanSummary.title: DdmrpPlanSummary
DdmrpPlanSummary.description:
The plan's counts: the rows with an order signal and the rows
per on-hand status (the "ok" rows count in none of them).

DdmrpZoneResponse.title: DdmrpZoneResponse
DdmrpZoneResponse.description: The zones of every designated item-site, as of one date.

DdmrpZoneRow.title: DdmrpZoneRow
DdmrpZoneRow.description:
One designated item-site's DDMRP buffer zones.

The zone fields (those of ``app.ddmrp.zones.buffer_zones``) are
null for a row whose status is not "ok".  ``adu_base`` is the
unadjusted ADU and ``adjustment_factor`` the active adjustment
factor on the as-of date (1.0 when no adjustment window covers
it); ``adu`` is ``adu_base`` times that factor, and the zone
fields are the ``buffer_zones`` of the adjusted ADU.

DecisionBody.title: DecisionBody
DecisionBody.description:
The body of POST /api/drift/decisions.

Every business rule is a model validation, so a rejected body
answers 422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope, exactly like
a malformed one.

DecisionSummaryResponse.title: DecisionSummaryResponse
DecisionSummaryResponse.description:
The response of GET /api/decisions/summary: the three kinds and
their bucket-by-bucket sum in ``total``.

DeferralCandidate.title: DeferralCandidate
DeferralCandidate.description: One planned order arriving in an over-budget month.

DeferralCandidates.title: DeferralCandidates
DeferralCandidates.description: The deferral candidates of the over-budget months of the horizon.

DeferralMonth.title: DeferralMonth
DeferralMonth.description: One over-budget month and the deferrals estimated for it.

DemandEventResponse.title: DemandEventResponse
DemandEventResponse.description: Response model for a stored demand event row.

DemandSignalBody.title: DemandSignalBody
DemandSignalBody.description:
The body of POST /api/demand-signals.

``kind`` is "promotion", "deal" or "event"; ``start_date`` after
the shared default as-of date, ``end_date`` not before
``start_date`` and not past the last day of the 12 forecast
periods at that as-of date; ``quantity`` above 0, finite and at
most 1,000,000,000; ``reason`` non-blank, at most 1,000
characters, stored trimmed.  Every business refusal answers 422
with a sentence in ``detail`` and nothing is stored; extra
fields answer 422.

DemandSignalRow.title: DemandSignalRow
DemandSignalRow.description:
One stored demand signal, or the stored row of its withdrawal.

A signal row carries ``withdrawn`` false and null
``withdrawn_*`` values while it stands; once withdrawn it carries
the withdrawal's values.  A withdrawal row answers its own POST
with ``withdrawn`` true and its own values beside it.
``created_by_name`` is the caller's display name as the decision
tables store it, through the shared
``app.auth.display_name.display_name`` helper — never null on a
row the API stored; it stays nullable only for rows written out
of band.

DemandSignalWithdrawalBody.title: DemandSignalWithdrawalBody
DemandSignalWithdrawalBody.description:
The body of POST /api/demand-signals/{id}/withdraw.

A blank or over-1,000-character reason answers 422 with nothing
stored.  An unknown id answers 404; an id that is itself a
withdrawal, an already withdrawn signal, and a signal whose
window has passed each answer 409.

DemandStatsResponse.title: DemandStatsResponse
DemandStatsResponse.description: One item-site's demand profile over its 30-day buckets.

DraftPoAction.title: DraftPoAction
DraftPoAction.description:
One stored draft-PO confirm audit row.

``created_at`` is the ISO-8601 rendering of the row's timestamptz
column; ``actor_name``, ``target_item_code``, ``target_site_code``,
``target_supplier_code``, ``odoo_id``, ``odoo_name`` and
``error_class`` are null wherever the row does not carry them (the
target codes are null only on rows written before the target
columns existed).

DraftPoBody.title: DraftPoBody
DraftPoBody.description:
Payload for the draft purchase order action.

The three codes must be non-empty, NUL-free strings of at most
255 characters; ``quantity`` must be a number strictly greater
than zero and ``unit_price`` a number greater than or equal to
zero (a violation is a 422).
``confirm`` defaults to false: the request only previews what a
confirm would do. The route never accepts a caller-supplied origin.

DriftDecisionRow.title: DriftDecisionRow
DriftDecisionRow.description:
A drift row enriched with the item-site's current planner decision.

``decision`` is the item-site's current decision from
``planner_decisions`` (the latest row by ``decided_at``, ``id``
breaking ties — the same row ``GET /api/drift/decisions`` reports
as current) with every stored column, or null when the item-site
has none.  ``decision_lapsed`` is true only while the current
decision is a dismissal whose ``recommended_reorder_point_units``
differs from the row's ``reorder_point_units`` by at least the
larger of 1 and 10% of that recommended value; it is false for
every other case, including rows with no decision.

``demand_basis`` names the basis (the ``replenishment.demand_basis``
value) the recommendation's reorder point was built on, and
``other_basis`` holds the other basis' whole-unit results (see
``DriftOtherBasis``) — null when the recommendation's
``other_basis`` is.  ``order_quantity`` is the recommendation's
recommended order quantity (see ``OrderQuantity``) — null when
the recommendation's is.  ``service_level_source`` names where the
recommendation's service level came from (see
``ServiceLevelSource``) and ``service_level`` is that service
level — the recommendation's ``inputs["service_level"]`` — null
when the recommendation carries no ``service_level_source`` or no
``inputs`` ``service_level``.

DriftOtherBasis.title: DriftOtherBasis
DriftOtherBasis.description:
The other demand basis' whole-unit results of the recommendation.

The drift row's view of the recommendation's ``other_basis``:
``basis`` is ``"history"`` or ``"forecast"`` — the basis that is
not the recommendation's active one — and ``reorder_point_units``
and ``safety_stock_units`` are that basis' whole-unit results, the
same values the recommendation's ``other_basis`` carries for them.

EmpiricalAdoption.title: EmpiricalAdoption
EmpiricalAdoption.description: One stored empirical adoption for an item-site.

EmpiricalAdoptionBody.title: EmpiricalAdoptionBody
EmpiricalAdoptionBody.description:
The body of PUT /api/empirical-adoptions.

Every business rule is a model validation, so a rejected body
answers 422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope, exactly like
a malformed one.

EmpiricalReorderPoint.title: EmpiricalReorderPoint
EmpiricalReorderPoint.description:
The empirical lead-time demand reorder point of one item-site.

The eleven keys of the
``app.recommend.empirical.empirical_reorder_point`` result: the
service-level quantile of the overlapping lead-time-day demand
spans of the pair's daily totals, from the demand row's
``daily_window_start`` to the as-of. ``window_days`` is the lead
time in whole days, ``spans`` the number of overlapping spans and
``spans_with_demand`` how many of them are positive;
``reorder_point`` its whole-unit ``reorder_point_units``,
``mean_lead_time_demand`` the mean span total and
``safety_stock`` (with its whole-unit ``safety_stock_units``)
``max(0, reorder_point - mean_lead_time_demand)``.

ErpCurrenciesResponse.title: ErpCurrenciesResponse
ErpCurrenciesResponse.description:
The answer of ``GET /api/erp-currencies``.

``reporting_currency`` is the ``erp.reporting_currency`` system
setting (the stored value when it is one of the allowed currencies,
ignoring case, else the registry default) and ``sources`` one entry
per stored row of ``erp_source_currencies``, ordered by source
system then code — empty while no row is stored.

ErpMappingIn.title: ErpMappingIn
ErpMappingIn.description:
The body of PUT /api/erp-mappings.

``kind`` is one of item/site/vendor, ``target_system`` is odoo, and
both codes are non-blank, NUL-free strings of at most 255
characters.

ErpMappingOut.title: ErpMappingOut
ErpMappingOut.description: One stored mapping as served by the erp-mappings routes.

ErpMappingSuggestion.title: ErpMappingSuggestion
ErpMappingSuggestion.description:
One item-mapping suggestion as served by
``GET /api/erp-mappings/suggestions``.

``source_code`` is the Acumatica code and ``target_code`` the Odoo
code, the way ``erp_code_mappings`` stores ``kind`` ``item`` with
``target_system`` ``odoo``.  ``matched_on`` is ``code`` (the same
item code held in ``item_sites`` under both systems, at different
sites) or ``description`` (the descriptions equal after trimming
and ignoring case); ``ambiguous`` is true when one code's
description matched several codes on the other side.  The
descriptions are the stored values, null when the code has no
``inventory_items`` row under its side.

ErpSource.title: ErpSource
ErpSource.description:
One source system's footprint in item_sites.

``source_system`` is the source's code or null, ``item_sites`` the
number of item-sites it stores and ``last_synced_at`` the newest
``synced_at`` of its rows.

ErpSourceCurrency.title: ErpSourceCurrency
ErpSourceCurrency.description:
One stored row of ``erp_source_currencies``.

``source_system`` the source system's code, ``currency_code`` the
uppercase ISO-4217 code it reports in and ``seen_at`` the newest
sync that saw the code (ISO-8601).

ErpSourceItemSite.title: ErpSourceItemSite
ErpSourceItemSite.description:
One item-site: the (item_code, site_code) pair and the source
system that stores it (a code or null).

ErpSourcesResponse.title: ErpSourcesResponse
ErpSourcesResponse.description:
The answer of ``GET /api/erp-sources``.

``sources`` is ordered by ``item_sites`` descending, then
``source_system`` with null last; ``item_sites`` by ``item_code``,
then ``site_code``.

ErpStandingGrantIn.title: ErpStandingGrantIn
ErpStandingGrantIn.description:
The body of POST /api/standing-grants.

``process`` is one of the two release process names, both values
a finite number above 0 and at most ``VALUE_MAX`` inclusive with
``max_daily_value`` not below ``max_document_value``, and
``max_data_age_hours`` a whole number from 1 to 168.  A field the
model does not name is rejected as well.  Anything else is
rejected with a 422 before anything is written.

ErpStandingGrantOut.title: ErpStandingGrantOut
ErpStandingGrantOut.description: One stored standing grant as served by the routes.

ErpStandingGrantRunLeftOut.title: ErpStandingGrantRunLeftOut
ErpStandingGrantRunLeftOut.description:
One group a run's limits left out, as the run stored it.

``site_code`` and ``supplier_code`` name the group, ``value`` the
number the entry's stored decimal string reads as and ``reason``
the limit that left the group out (``document_limit`` or
``daily_limit``).

ErpStandingGrantRunOut.title: ErpStandingGrantRunOut
ErpStandingGrantRunOut.description:
One stored standing-grant run as served by
``GET /api/standing-grants/runs``.

``process`` and ``grant_id`` the run's process and the grant in
force it ran under, ``started_at`` the ISO-8601 string with its
UTC offset, ``outcome`` the run's outcome, ``reason`` why the run
did not release (null when the run has none), ``documents`` the
count and ``value`` the summed value of the groups it sent and
``left_out`` the groups its limits left out, in their stored
order.

ErpStandingGrantTransferRunLeftOut.title: ErpStandingGrantTransferRunLeftOut
ErpStandingGrantTransferRunLeftOut.description:
One transfer group a run's limits left out, as the run stored
it.

``from_site`` and ``to_site`` name the group's pair, ``value``
the number the entry's stored decimal string reads as (the
summed value of the suggestions that have one for a
``no_value`` entry) and ``reason`` the limit that left the group
out (``no_value``, ``document_limit`` or ``daily_limit``).

ExceptionCounts.title: ExceptionCounts
ExceptionCounts.description:
The response's row counts: by severity, by stored
acknowledgement and the rows whose ``new`` is true.  The counts
cover only the rows returned.

ExceptionResponse.title: ExceptionResponse
ExceptionResponse.description: The exceptions triage list, as of the latest source as-of.

ExceptionRow.title: ExceptionRow
ExceptionRow.description:
One exception: a row of the triage list.

``key`` is the stable ``<kind>:<ref>`` identity; ``item_code``
and ``site_code`` are null when the exception is not
item-specific; ``view`` is the planner hash that shows it and
``detected_on`` the date the exception was detected.
``first_seen_on`` is the date the key was first captured (null
when it has never been captured) and ``new`` is true only when
``first_seen_on`` equals the response's as-of date.

ExcessDecision.title: ExcessDecision
ExcessDecision.description: One stored excess decision on an item-site's ranked row.

ExcessDecisionBody.title: ExcessDecisionBody
ExcessDecisionBody.description:
The body of POST /api/excess/decisions.

Every business rule is a model validation, so a rejected body
answers 422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope, exactly like
a malformed one.

ExcessDecisionRow.title: ExcessDecisionRow
ExcessDecisionRow.description:
An excess row enriched with the item-site's current decision.

``decision`` is the item-site's current decision from
``excess_decisions`` (the latest row by ``decided_at``, ``id``
breaking ties — the same row ``GET /api/excess/decisions`` reports
as current) with every stored column, or null when the item-site
has none.  ``decision_lapsed`` is true only for a current
dismissal that the row has outgrown: the row's ``excess_units``
exceed the decision's ``excess_units`` by at least the larger of 1
and 10% of the decision's ``excess_units``.  A snooze never lapses,
and neither does anything else (accepted decisions, or no decision
at all).

ExcessProposalBucket.title: ExcessProposalBucket
ExcessProposalBucket.description:
One remedy kind's two counts among the current accepted
excess decisions: the decisions proposed the kind and the
decisions that chose it.

ExcessProposalCounts.title: ExcessProposalCounts
ExcessProposalCounts.description:
The stored remedy proposals of the current accepted excess
decisions.

ExcessRemedy.title: ExcessRemedy
ExcessRemedy.description:
The one remedy proposed for an excess row.

``kind`` is the remedy's kind — one of the excess decision's own
action values (``stop_replenishing``, ``reduce`` or ``dispose``).
``on_order_units`` is the sum of the open purchase lines'
``open_units`` for the row's item-site that are finite numbers
above 0 (0 when no line counts, whatever the lines' promised
dates); ``current_reorder_point`` and ``current_max_qty`` the
row's item-site's ``item_sites`` levels (each null when the
item-site has no ``item_sites`` row or the value is null or not a
finite number); ``reason`` is the one line of text for why the
remedy fits the row.

ExpediteLine.title: ExpediteLine
ExpediteLine.description:
One open purchase line to expedite.

``order_type``, ``order_nbr`` and ``line_nbr`` come from the line's
business key ``OrderType:OrderNbr:LineNbr`` (null when the key is
too short to carry them). ``open_value`` is null without an
item-site unit cost, ``days_late`` is null when the line is not
late, and ``d``, ``days_of_cover`` and ``projected_stockout_on``
are null when the item-site has no "ok" recommendation with daily
demand above 0.

ExpediteResponse.title: ExpediteResponse
ExpediteResponse.description:
Open purchase lines to expedite for the as-of date.

``lines`` rank by soonest projected stockout (no projected date
last), then larger days late, then larger open value, then order
and line number; ``stale_excluded`` counts the undated lines and
the lines promised more than 90 days before ``as_of`` that are
left out of the list.

FeedStatusResponse.title: FeedStatusResponse
FeedStatusResponse.description: Freshness of the five feed tables and the data horizon.

ForecastBacktest.title: ForecastBacktest
ForecastBacktest.description: The winning method's one-bucket-ahead backtest score.

ForecastBucket.title: ForecastBucket
ForecastBucket.description:
One 30-day bucket: its boundaries, its statistical quantity,
and the effective forecast beside it.

``quantity`` is the statistical forecast, never changed by any
override [rule: OVR-4].  ``effective_quantity`` is the sum of the
bucket's day shares — one day's share of the counted override
covering each day, else one day's share of the statistical
quantity — and ``override_days`` how many of the bucket's days an
override covers, from 0 to the bucket's length.

ForecastRow.title: ForecastRow
ForecastRow.description:
One item-site's forecast: the method, the 12 buckets, the backtest.

``total_forecast`` and ``forecast`` are the statistical
forecast's, unchanged by any override [rule: OVR-4]; beside them,
``total_effective_forecast`` is the sum of the buckets'
``effective_quantity`` and ``overridden_buckets`` how many of the
buckets have at least one overridden day.

ForecastRowDetail.title: ForecastRowDetail
ForecastRowDetail.description: A forecast row plus the history buckets it was built from.

GuidanceGetOut.title: GuidanceGetOut
GuidanceGetOut.description:
The answer of GET /api/guidance.

Exactly two keys: ``publication`` (null when nothing was ever
published) and ``items`` (the current versions — the
``guidance_versions`` rows whose ``last_publication_id`` is the
publication's id; empty when nothing was ever published) — in
the route's own order, which the route sorts: by type in the
order direction, boundary, roadmap, design; within a type by the
number at the end of the key, compared as a number and
ascending; and for the same number by the key in Unicode code
point order.  The fixed field set is serialized with explicit
null values; no extra field is ever emitted.

GuidanceIn.title: GuidanceIn
GuidanceIn.description:
The body of PUT /api/guidance: the whole guidance.

``source`` is plain text of 1 to 120 characters (what was
published, a commit or a label) and ``items`` a list of 1 to 2000
items; no key appears twice in one body.  Anything else is
rejected with a 422 before anything is written.

GuidanceItemHistoryOut.title: GuidanceItemHistoryOut
GuidanceItemHistoryOut.description:
The answer of GET /api/guidance/items/{key}.

``key`` is the key asked for, ``current`` true when one of the
item's versions is current (its ``last_publication_id`` is the id
of the newest publication) and ``versions`` every
``guidance_versions`` row with that key, the newest first (by row
``id``, descending).

GuidanceItemIn.title: GuidanceItemIn
GuidanceItemIn.description:
One item of the guidance body.

Every field must validate or the whole publication is refused with
a 422 before anything is written (one wrong item refuses the whole
publication).  The stored text is exactly the string that was
sent.

GuidanceItemOut.title: GuidanceItemOut
GuidanceItemOut.description:
One current version, as served by GET /api/guidance.

``stamp`` is the key, the character ``@`` and the hash — the
stamp that names this exact version.  ``decided_under``,
``decided_ref`` and ``authority`` are null when the version was
published without them.  ``since`` is the ``published_at`` of the
publication the row's ``first_publication_id`` names (an
ISO-8601 string with a UTC offset): the moment AIERP first held
this version.

GuidanceOut.title: GuidanceOut
GuidanceOut.description:
The answer of PUT /api/guidance.

``changed`` is false when nothing was written; ``publication_id``
is the id of the newest publication after the call; ``items`` the
number of items in the body; ``new_versions`` the version rows
inserted; ``withdrawn`` the keys that were current before the call
and are not in the body.

GuidancePublicationOut.title: GuidancePublicationOut
GuidancePublicationOut.description:
The newest publication, as served by GET /api/guidance.

``id`` is the row's id (the highest, the newest), ``source`` the
text as stored, ``published_at`` the moment the row was written
(an ISO-8601 string with a UTC offset), ``published_by`` the
publisher's username (or ``deployment``) and ``item_count`` the
number of items the publication held.

GuidancePublicationRefOut.title: GuidancePublicationRefOut
GuidancePublicationRefOut.description:
The publication one version row's end names.

``publication_id`` is the row's id in ``guidance_publications``,
``source`` the text as stored, ``published_at`` the moment the row
was written (an ISO-8601 string with a UTC offset) and
``published_by`` the publisher's username (or ``deployment``).

GuidanceStampOut.title: GuidanceStampOut
GuidanceStampOut.description:
The answer of GET /api/guidance/stamps/{stamp}.

``stamp`` is the key, the character ``@`` and the hash, ``key``
and ``hash`` its parts and ``type``, ``title`` and
``statement`` the words the stamp names.  ``current`` is true
when a row with that key and hash is current, ``superseded`` true
when the key has a current row with another hash, and
``versions`` every ``guidance_versions`` row with that key and
hash, the newest first (by row ``id``, descending).

GuidanceVersionOut.title: GuidanceVersionOut
GuidanceVersionOut.description:
One version row, as the two history routes serve it.

``stamp`` is the key, the character ``@`` and the hash — the
stamp that names this exact version.  ``decided_on`` is the
row's date as a ``YYYY-MM-DD`` string; ``decided_under``,
``decided_ref`` and ``authority`` are null when the version was
published without them.  ``current`` is true when the row's
``last_publication_id`` is the id of the newest publication.
``first`` and ``last`` describe the publications the row's
``first_publication_id`` and ``last_publication_id`` name.

HistoryBucket.title: HistoryBucket
HistoryBucket.description:
One of the 30-day history buckets a forecast was built from.

The history carries its three fields only — ``bucket_start``,
``bucket_end`` and ``quantity``; the effective forecast applies
to the forecast buckets, never to the history.

IntermittentImpactResponse.title: IntermittentImpactResponse
IntermittentImpactResponse.description:
The response of ``GET /api/recommendations/intermittent-impact``:
the summary plus one row per intermittent or lumpy item-site whose
``empirical`` reorder point is not null, ordered by ``item_code``
then ``site_code``.  The rows describe what the
``replenishment.intermittent_recommendations`` switch does, not
whether it is on: the same rows are served with the switch on or
off.

IntermittentImpactRow.title: IntermittentImpactRow
IntermittentImpactRow.description:
One intermittent or lumpy item-site's empirical reorder point
impact, as served by ``GET /api/recommendations/intermittent-impact``.

``item_code`` and ``site_code`` name the item-site,
``demand_class`` the result's ``"intermittent"`` or ``"lumpy"``
and ``unit_cost`` the unit cost carried from item_sites (null
when absent). ``current_reorder_point`` the result's
``current.reorder_point`` (null when absent),
``empirical_reorder_point_units`` the
``empirical.reorder_point_units``,
``reorder_point_units_delta`` the empirical units minus the
current reorder point (a null current counts as 0),
``dollar_delta`` that delta times the unit cost, null when the
unit cost is absent or not positive, and ``adopted`` whether the
item-site has a stored empirical adoption (the result's
``empirical_adopted``) — carried by the endpoint only when the
``recommendations_for_all`` call read the stored adoptions and
absent from the row otherwise: a value the call did not read is
not masked as false.

IntermittentImpactSummary.title: IntermittentImpactSummary
IntermittentImpactSummary.description:
The summary of the empirical reorder point impact.

``item_sites`` the number of rows, ``current_value`` and
``empirical_value`` the sums of current reorder point times unit
cost and of empirical units times unit cost over the rows with a
positive unit cost (each rounded to cents), ``dollar_delta``
``empirical_value`` minus ``current_value``,
``item_sites_without_unit_cost`` the rows whose unit cost is
absent, zero or negative and ``switch_on`` the stored or default
value of the ``replenishment.intermittent_recommendations``
switch.

InventoryItemCreate.title: InventoryItemCreate
InventoryItemCreate.description: Payload for creating an inventory item.

InventoryItemResponse.title: InventoryItemResponse
InventoryItemResponse.description: Response model for an inventory item record.

InventoryItemUpdate.title: InventoryItemUpdate
InventoryItemUpdate.description: Payload for updating an inventory item; every field optional.

ItemLeadTimeStats.title: ItemLeadTimeStats
ItemLeadTimeStats.description: One item's pooled lead time stats with the per-supplier breakdown.

ItemSiteResponse.title: ItemSiteResponse
ItemSiteResponse.description: Response model for a stored item/site row.

KindSummary.title: KindSummary
KindSummary.description:
The summary of one decision kind (drift, excess, stockout or
total): ``accepted`` equals ``applied`` plus ``outstanding`` in
count and money.

LeadTimeObservationResponse.title: LeadTimeObservationResponse
LeadTimeObservationResponse.description: Response model for a stored lead time observation row.

OnHandResponse.title: OnHandResponse
OnHandResponse.description: Response model for a stored on_hand row.

OrderPlanReleaseIn.title: OrderPlanReleaseIn
OrderPlanReleaseIn.description:
The order-plan release body.

``horizon_days`` is the supply-plan horizon (1 to 60, default 7),
``supplier_codes`` the non-empty list of up to 50 supplier codes —
each 1 to 64 characters, no NUL bytes — ``top_ups`` the (default
empty) list of at most 200 chosen top-ups — each exactly
``supplier_code``, ``item_code`` and ``site_code``, each 1 to 64
characters without NUL bytes, repeated entries counting once, and
each entry's ``supplier_code`` one of ``supplier_codes`` (a code
that is not is refused with 422, naming that code) — and
``confirm`` the preview/confirm flag (default false).  Any extra
field is refused with 422, like every other body in the app; a
missing body is 422 by request validation.

OrderPlanTopUpEntry.title: OrderPlanTopUpEntry
OrderPlanTopUpEntry.description:
One chosen top-up of the order-plan release body: the supplier,
the item and the site — exactly the keys the top-up suggestions
hold.  Each field is 1 to 64 characters without NUL bytes, and any
extra field is refused with 422, like every other body in the app.

OrderQuantity.title: OrderQuantity
OrderQuantity.description:
The recommended order quantity of a recommendable item-site.

``basis`` is ``"eoq"`` (the economic order quantity from the
item-site's ``unit_cost``, per-order cost and annual holding rate)
or ``"assumed_30_days"`` (30 days of demand when the unit cost is
absent or not positive); ``clamped`` is ``"min_cover"`` or
``"max_cover"`` when the quantity was clamped to 7 or 365 days of
demand, else null. ``order_quantity`` is the exact float after
clamping, ``order_quantity_units`` its whole-unit ceiling (at
least 1) and ``cover_days`` the days of demand those units cover.
``recommended_max_units`` is the recommended reorder point in
whole units plus ``order_quantity_units``; ``current_order_qty``
and ``current_max_qty`` are the item-site's current ``order_qty``
and ``max_qty`` from item_sites (null when absent).

OtherBasis.title: OtherBasis
OtherBasis.description:
The reorder point the other demand basis would give.

``basis`` is ``"history"`` or ``"forecast"`` — the basis that is
not the active one; the rest are that basis' exact results and
inputs.

OverrideBody.title: OverrideBody
OverrideBody.description:
The body of POST /api/forecast/overrides.

``period_start`` must be the first day of one of the 12 forecast
periods at the shared default as-of date; the stored
``period_end`` is that period's last day.  Every business
refusal (a blank or over-long reason, a negative or non-finite
quantity, a period outside the current horizon, an item-site
with no statistical forecast) answers 422 with a sentence in
``detail``, and nothing is stored.

OverrideRow.title: OverrideRow
OverrideRow.description:
One stored forecast override or withdrawal, plus ``applies``.

``applies`` is true only for an ``override`` row that is the
current row of its period (the highest ``id`` for that
item-site and ``period_start``).  ``created_by_name`` is the
caller's display name as the decision tables store it, through
the shared ``app.auth.display_name.display_name`` helper — the
token's username, else its email, else its subject — never null
on a row the API stored; it stays nullable only for rows written
out of band.

ParameterWriteback.title: ParameterWriteback
ParameterWriteback.description:
One parameter-writeback audit row (append-only).

The parameter values are carried as exact decimals: the binary
floats of the Float columns are rendered through their shortest
round-trip representation, so 0.1000 comes back exactly 0.1 —
never a 17-digit binary-float artifact.

ParameterWritebackConfirmBody.title: ParameterWritebackConfirmBody
ParameterWritebackConfirmBody.description:
The body of POST /api/parameter-writeback/confirm.

1 to 200 item-site pairs, no duplicate pair — an empty list, more
than 200 items, or a duplicate (item_code, site_code) pair
answers 422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope (raised in
the field constraint and the validator below).

ParameterWritebackConfirmItem.title: ParameterWritebackConfirmItem
ParameterWritebackConfirmItem.description:
One requested item-site pair of the confirm body.

A NUL byte in either code, or a code over 64 characters, answers
422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope (raised in the
validator below) instead of reaching the database.

ParameterWritebackConfirmResponse.title: ParameterWritebackConfirmResponse
ParameterWritebackConfirmResponse.description:
The response of POST /api/parameter-writeback/confirm: the
per-pair results in request order and the outcome counts.

ParameterWritebackConfirmResult.title: ParameterWritebackConfirmResult
ParameterWritebackConfirmResult.description:
One confirm result, in request order.

``reason`` is null for a written or unchanged write, "not
outstanding" or the row's blocked_reason for a skipped pair, and
the stable public reason "writer_error" for a failed write —
never the exception's class name, message, or provider
internals.  ``before`` and ``after`` are null for a skipped or
failed pair.

ParameterWritebackConfirmValues.title: ParameterWritebackConfirmValues
ParameterWritebackConfirmValues.description:
The before or after values of one confirm result: the
item-site's parameter fields, mirroring the preview's numeric
shape, serialized as JSON numbers — ``order_qty`` is null when
the derived value (max minus reorder point) is not positive.

ParameterWritebackPreviewResponse.title: ParameterWritebackPreviewResponse
ParameterWritebackPreviewResponse.description:
The response of GET /api/parameter-writeback/preview: the rows
(money at stake descending, nulls last, then item and site) and
the totals.

ParameterWritebackRow.title: ParameterWritebackRow
ParameterWritebackRow.description:
One preview row: the outstanding accepted decision, the
item-site's current parameters and the proposed writeback values.

PlanReleaseRow.title: PlanReleaseRow
PlanReleaseRow.description: One stored plan_releases audit row, every column of it.

PlannerDecision.title: PlannerDecision
PlannerDecision.description: One stored planner decision on an item-site's drift row.

ProjectionBucket.title: ProjectionBucket
ProjectionBucket.description: One calendar-month bucket of one site's projection.

ProjectionGroup.title: ProjectionGroup
ProjectionGroup.description: One site's projection: its buckets and its item-sites without a unit cost.

ProjectionGroupKey.title: ProjectionGroupKey
ProjectionGroupKey.description: The grouping dimension and its code.

PurchaseBudgetIn.title: PurchaseBudgetIn
PurchaseBudgetIn.description:
The amount of PUT /api/purchase-budgets/{month}.

``amount`` is the month's budget: a finite number between
``AMOUNT_MIN`` and ``AMOUNT_MAX`` inclusive.  A negative or
non-finite number (the ge/le constraints refuse NaN and the
infinities), one above the cap, a string, a boolean, a null or a
missing body is rejected with a 422 before anything is written.

PurchaseBudgetOut.title: PurchaseBudgetOut
PurchaseBudgetOut.description: One stored purchase budget as served by the purchase-budgets routes.

RecommendationChangeRow.title: RecommendationChangeRow
RecommendationChangeRow.description:
One item-site's reorder-point change between since and as_of.

``contributions`` (with ``primary_driver``) and the ``inputs_then`` /
``inputs_now`` input sets are null when either side is not an "ok"
recommendation; the reorder point, unit ceiling and ``change_units``
are null on the side that is not "ok", and ``money`` is null without
a positive unit cost and ``change_units``.

RecommendationInputs.title: RecommendationInputs
RecommendationInputs.description: The inputs substituted into the recommendation formulas.

RecommendationResponse.title: RecommendationResponse
RecommendationResponse.description:
One item-site's reorder point recommendation.

``demand_basis`` names the basis (the ``replenishment.demand_basis``
value) the other fields were built on; ``other_basis`` holds the
other basis' reorder point and is null when the recommendation's
status is not ``ok`` or the other basis does not exist.
``service_level_source`` names where the service level came from
(the item-site's ABC class when the
``replenishment.service_level_by_class`` switch is on and the
item-site is classified, else the single service level).
``on_hand_units`` is the item-site's ``on_hand`` quantity (0 when
it has no on_hand row), ``on_order_units`` the sum of the item-site's
open purchase lines' ``open_units`` (0 when none), ``unit_cost`` the
``unit_cost`` carried from the item_sites row (null when absent),
``source_system`` the ``source_system`` stored on the item_sites
row (null when absent) and ``suggested_order_quantity``
``max(0, reorder_point_units - (on_hand_units + on_order_units))``
for a recommendable item-site, null when the recommendation has no
``reorder_point_units`` (a stopped, excess-only or otherwise
non-recommendable item-site). ``order_quantity`` is the
item-site's recommended order quantity (an
:class:`OrderQuantity`) for a recommendable item-site, null
otherwise.  ``empirical_adopted`` is true when the item-site has
a stored empirical adoption (one row of ``empirical_adoptions``
for the pair) and false otherwise — an adopted item-site is
recommended on its ``empirical`` reorder point with the
``replenishment.intermittent_recommendations`` switch off as on.

``signal_units`` is the item-site's counted demand signals' units
over the lead-time window (0 when none, and 0 on a not-ok row)
and ``reorder_point_before_signals_units`` the row's
``reorder_point_units`` before those units were added to
``reorder_point`` (null on a not-ok row).

``on_hand_units``, ``on_order_units`` and ``suggested_order_quantity``
are strict whole units: a true ``int`` or null only. An integer-
valued float or a ``Decimal`` is not a unit count and is rejected
rather than coerced.

ReleaseGroup.title: ReleaseGroup
ReleaseGroup.description:
One (site, supplier) group of the release plan.

``outcome``, ``warehouse_code``, ``vendor_code``, ``order_nbr`` and
``error`` are null in the bare plan and after a preview with an
incomplete Acumatica configuration; the preview fills them from
the client's per-order result, a confirm from its batch.

ReleaseIn.title: ReleaseIn
ReleaseIn.description:
The release body: the month and the confirm flag.

Any extra field is refused with 422, like every other body in the
app; a missing body is 422 by request validation.

ReleaseLine.title: ReleaseLine
ReleaseLine.description:
One line of one release group, exactly as sent to Acumatica.

The monetary fields are exact decimals — the planned order's
values, never binary floats — rendered as decimal strings in the
JSON body.

ReleasePlan.title: ReleasePlan
ReleasePlan.description: The release plan with the per-group Acumatica outcomes on top.

ReleaseTrackingCounts.title: ReleaseTrackingCounts
ReleaseTrackingCounts.description:
The fixed state counts of the tracking view.

Exactly these four keys, each an integer, no more and no fewer:
``partly_received`` counts the ``partially_received`` state.

ReleaseTrackingLine.title: ReleaseTrackingLine
ReleaseTrackingLine.description:
One order line as Acumatica reports it.

``order_qty`` and ``received_qty`` are the ordered and the on-
receipt (``QtyOnReceipts``) quantities, and ``promised`` the
line's promised date as an ISO calendar date, or null.

ReleaseTrackingOrder.title: ReleaseTrackingOrder
ReleaseTrackingOrder.description:
One released order with its tracking state as of today.

``state`` is one of ``late``, ``awaiting_approval``,
``partially_received``, ``open``, ``received``, ``cancelled``,
``missing``, in that priority order.  ``days_waiting`` is the
whole days since the order's ERP date while it is on hold — null
when it is not on hold — and ``days_late`` is today minus the
earliest late line's expected date — null unless the state is
``late``.  ``expected_on`` is the earliest expected date of the
lines that are active, not completed and short of receipt, as an
ISO date, null when there is no such line, and
``promise_is_default`` is true when that earliest line's promise
is the ERP default, false when it is the supplier's own date —
both null together with ``expected_on``, judged from the
supplier performance read like Expedite (absent from the
order, and from the body, only when that read is refused — an
as_of after the server's today, which the route never asks
for).  ``value`` is the
release row's exact decimal, rendered as a decimal string in the
JSON body.

ReleaseTrackingView.title: ReleaseTrackingView
ReleaseTrackingView.description: The tracking view of every released order as of ``as_of``.

ScenarioCreate.title: ScenarioCreate
ScenarioCreate.description:
Payload for creating a scenario.

``name`` is a non-blank string of at most 200 characters; every
lever is optional — a null (or omitted) lever keeps the baseline
value, as in ``POST /api/scenarios/simulate``.

ScenarioResponse.title: ScenarioResponse
ScenarioResponse.description: Response model for a stored scenario.

ScenarioUpdate.title: ScenarioUpdate
ScenarioUpdate.description:
Payload for partially updating a scenario; every field optional.

An omitted field is left unchanged; an explicit null for a lever
clears it to the baseline value (the column stores null).  A
``name`` that is given must be a non-blank string, as on create —
an explicit null is rejected (a 422), because a stored name is
never null.

SecondSourceCandidate.title: SecondSourceCandidate
SecondSourceCandidate.description:
One other supplier's terms row, or a similar-item supplier, for
a sole-source item.

SecondSourceEntry.title: SecondSourceEntry
SecondSourceEntry.description:
One sole-source item of one risk entry, with its candidates and
its bridge stock.

SecondSourceResponse.title: SecondSourceResponse
SecondSourceResponse.description:
Second-source candidates for the sole-source items, as of the
risk answer's as-of.

ServiceLevelClass.title: ServiceLevelClass
ServiceLevelClass.description:
One ABC class' entry of the curve.

``abc_class`` is ``"A"``, ``"B"`` or ``"C"``, ``item_sites`` the
class' counted item-sites (0 for a class with none, whose points'
sums are 0), ``fill_rate_item_sites`` the class' counted
item-sites that take part in the fill rate (the ones whose
``order_quantity`` is an object whose ``order_quantity`` is a
finite number above 0; 0 when none takes part, whose points'
``expected_fill_rate`` is null) and ``current_level`` the class'
current service level (its stored or default class level with the
``replenishment.service_level_by_class`` switch on, the single
service level with it off).

ServiceLevelCurveResponse.title: ServiceLevelCurveResponse
ServiceLevelCurveResponse.description:
The safety-stock cost curve of the service levels, per ABC class.

``as_of`` is the first counted item-site's as-of (null when no row
counts), ``by_class`` the value of the
``replenishment.service_level_by_class`` switch,
``service_target`` the value of the
``replenishment.service_target`` setting (``fill_rate`` when the
stored value is ``fill_rate``, ``cycle`` otherwise — including
when nothing is stored), ``holding_rate`` the annual holding rate
the costs are computed at and ``classes`` one entry per class
``"A"``, ``"B"``, ``"C"``, in that order.

ServiceLevelPoint.title: ServiceLevelPoint
ServiceLevelPoint.description:
One service level's point of a class' curve.

``level`` is the service level (the z of the level is
``statistics.NormalDist().inv_cdf(level)``), ``safety_stock_units``
the sum over the class' counted item-sites of z times sigma, each
rounded up to a whole number, ``safety_stock_value`` the sum of z
times sigma times ``unit_cost`` rounded to 2 places,
``holding_cost`` that value times the holding rate rounded to 2
places and ``holding_cost_delta`` the difference to the previous
point's ``holding_cost`` (null for the first point);
``expected_fill_rate`` is 1 minus the sum over the taking-part
item-sites (the counted ones whose ``order_quantity`` is an object
whose ``order_quantity`` is a finite number above 0, its Q) of
sigma times G(z) times the yearly demand D (365 times
``inputs.d``) divided by Q, divided by the sum of their D, where
G(z) is the standard normal loss function — the standard normal
density at z minus z times one minus the standard normal
distribution at z — clamped to between 0 and 1 and rounded to 4
places (null when no item-site of the class takes part or their D
sums to 0); ``current`` is true only at the class' current level.

ServiceLevelSource.title: ServiceLevelSource
ServiceLevelSource.description:
Where the recommendation's service level came from.

``abc_class`` is the item-site's ABC class (``"A"``, ``"B"`` or
``"C"``) when the ``replenishment.service_level_by_class`` switch
is on and the item-site is classified, else null; ``source`` is
``"class"`` when the class' stored or default level was used,
``"single"`` when the single service level was (the switch off, or
an unclassified item-site).

ServiceLevelSuggestionCombination.title: ServiceLevelSuggestionCombination
ServiceLevelSuggestionCombination.description:
One combination of per-class service levels.

``levels`` holds the level of each of the classes ``A``, ``B``
and ``C``; ``holding_cost`` is the sum of the three classes'
curve-point ``holding_cost`` at those levels, rounded to 2
places; ``expected_fill_rate`` is 1 minus the sum over the
taking-part rows of all three classes of each row's expected
shortage at its class' level (the term the curve's
``expected_fill_rate`` sums), divided by the sum of those rows'
yearly demand, clamped to between 0 and 1 and rounded to 4
places (null when no row takes part).  Both follow the service
target in force, exactly as the curve does.

ServiceLevelSuggestionLevels.title: ServiceLevelSuggestionLevels
ServiceLevelSuggestionLevels.description:
The levels of one combination of service levels: one per class.

``A``, ``B`` and ``C`` are the service level of the class ``A``,
``B`` and ``C`` item-sites in the combination — each taken from
that class' ladder as the curve builds it (0.90, 0.92, 0.95,
0.97, 0.98, 0.99 and 0.995 plus the class' current level when
that is not already one of them).

ServiceLevelSuggestionResponse.title: ServiceLevelSuggestionResponse
ServiceLevelSuggestionResponse.description:
The suggestion: the cheapest combination of per-class service
levels whose expected fill rate reaches the target.

``as_of``, ``service_target`` and ``holding_rate`` as the curve
reports them; ``target_fill_rate`` the requested target (a number
from 0.5 to 0.999); ``current`` the combination of the classes'
current levels; ``highest`` the combination of each class'
highest ladder level; ``suggested`` the combination with the
lowest holding cost among those whose expected fill rate is at
least the target, a tie going to the lower level for A, then for
B, then for C, and null when no combination reaches the target or
no row takes part; and ``holding_cost_delta`` the suggested
holding cost minus the current one rounded to 2 places (null when
``suggested`` is null).  The target comparison uses the unrounded
aggregate before rounding; the rounded 4-place
``expected_fill_rate`` is the response display value only.

SettingEntry.title: SettingEntry
SettingEntry.description: One registered setting as served by the settings routes.

SignalAccuracyItemSite.title: SignalAccuracyItemSite
SignalAccuracyItemSite.description:
One item-site's signal measures.

Only the compared buckets with a stored ``signal_quantity``
above 0 are summed in: ``before_total`` is each bucket's
effective quantity minus its signal quantity (the forecast
before the signals), ``after_total`` its effective quantity,
``signal_total`` its signal quantity, ``before_wape`` and
``after_wape`` the sums of their absolute differences from the
actuals over ``actual_total`` (null when it is 0), and
``value_added`` ``before_wape`` minus ``after_wape`` — positive
when the signals moved the forecast nearer the actuals.

SignalAccuracyResult.title: SignalAccuracyResult
SignalAccuracyResult.description:
The realised value of the stored demand signals.

Only completed snapshot buckets (``bucket_end`` on or before
``as_of`` — the shared default as-of date when absent) with a
stored ``signal_quantity`` above 0 are compared with the actual
demand of their range, the same way ``GET /api/forecast/accuracy``
compares; a bucket whose signal is null or 0 is left out.
``item_sites`` carries one entry per item-site with the same
measures, ordered by ``signal_total`` descending, then
``item_code`` and ``site_code``.

SimulateBasis.title: SimulateBasis
SimulateBasis.description: One basis' reorder point and safety stock with their whole-unit values.

SimulateBody.title: SimulateBody
SimulateBody.description:
The levers to apply; an omitted lever keeps the baseline value.

``service_level`` must be a number strictly between 0 and 1;
``demand_multiplier`` and ``lead_time_multiplier`` must be positive
finite numbers; ``service_level_by_class`` must map exactly the keys
"A", "B" and "C", each to a number strictly between 0 and 1.

``service_level_by_class`` is deliberately typed ``object``: any
given value then reaches the engine's ``_validate_levers``, so an
invalid value answers 422 with a string detail naming the lever,
never Pydantic's list detail.

SimulateItemSite.title: SimulateItemSite
SimulateItemSite.description: One simulated item-site: baseline vs scenario and the signed unit deltas.

SimulateLevers.title: SimulateLevers
SimulateLevers.description: The levers applied; null when a lever was not given.

SimulateResponse.title: SimulateResponse
SimulateResponse.description: The simulation result: the portfolio summary and one row per simulated item-site.

SimulateSummary.title: SimulateSummary
SimulateSummary.description:
The portfolio summary of the simulation.

``levers`` echoes the three single levers applied, each null when
not given; ``service_level_by_class`` echoes the given per-class
mapping (null when the lever was not given).

SnapshotCaptureBody.title: SnapshotCaptureBody
SnapshotCaptureBody.description:
The optional body of POST /api/forecast/snapshots.

``as_of`` selects the date to snapshot; absent (or null) the
shared default as-of date is used. A date later than today is a
business 422 in FastAPI's validation envelope, exactly like a
malformed one.

SnapshotResult.title: SnapshotResult
SnapshotResult.description:
The result of a snapshot capture.

``created`` is true when rows were stored; for a date that
already has a snapshot it is false and ``origin``, ``item_sites``
and ``rows`` describe the stored snapshot.

SnapshotSummary.title: SnapshotSummary
SnapshotSummary.description: One stored forecast snapshot: the snapshot-level fields only.

SopReviewForecast.title: SopReviewForecast
SopReviewForecast.description: The realised accuracy of the stored forecast snapshots.

SopReviewMonth.title: SopReviewMonth
SopReviewMonth.description: One horizon month of the S&OP review.

SopReviewResponse.title: SopReviewResponse
SopReviewResponse.description: The S&OP review of the horizon months.

SopReviewSinceSignoff.title: SopReviewSinceSignoff
SopReviewSinceSignoff.description:
The drift of the current review against the newest stored
sign-off of any month — the review's ``since_signoff`` field,
``None`` when no sign-off exists at all.  ``signed_by`` is the
row's ``actor_name`` (its ``actor`` when that is missing or blank)
and ``signed_as_of`` the row's figures' ``as_of`` (null when
absent); ``months`` holds one entry per month in both the review
and the stored figures' months, in the review's order.

SopReviewSinceSignoffMonth.title: SopReviewSinceSignoffMonth
SopReviewSinceSignoffMonth.description:
One horizon month that appears in both the current review and
the newest stored sign-off's figures: the current value minus the
stored one of each delta field, null when either value is null,
missing or not a finite number.

SopScenariosBaseline.title: SopScenariosBaseline
SopScenariosBaseline.description: The baseline (no-lever) comparison figures over the horizon.

SopScenariosResponse.title: SopScenariosResponse
SopScenariosResponse.description: The S&OP scenarios comparison of the horizon.

SopScenariosScenario.title: SopScenariosScenario
SopScenariosScenario.description:
One stored scenario compared against the baseline.

The figures are null when the scenario answers with an ``error``
(its levers make the projection raise ``ValueError``, or it carries
a lever the projection does not accept).

SopSignoff.title: SopSignoff
SopSignoff.description:
One stored sign-off with its figures — the S&OP review answer
the route computed on the server at sign-off time.

SopSignoffIn.title: SopSignoffIn
SopSignoffIn.description:
The sign-off body.

``month`` is the review month to sign (``YYYY-MM``), ``note`` an
optional note (at most 500 characters, no NUL bytes — a blank one
is stored as null) and ``months`` the review's horizon, default 3,
bounded 1 to 12 inclusive.  Any extra field is refused with 422,
like every other body in the app.

SopSignoffRow.title: SopSignoffRow
SopSignoffRow.description: A stored sign-off without its figures.

SpendAgainstBudget.title: SpendAgainstBudget
SpendAgainstBudget.description: The monthly spend of the projection against the stored budgets.

SpendMonth.title: SpendMonth
SpendMonth.description: One calendar month of the spend view against the stored budget.

StockoutDecision.title: StockoutDecision
StockoutDecision.description: One stored stockout decision on an item-site's ranked row.

StockoutDecisionBody.title: StockoutDecisionBody
StockoutDecisionBody.description:
The body of POST /api/stockout/decisions.

Every business rule is a model validation, so a rejected body
answers 422 in FastAPI's HTTPValidationError envelope, exactly like
a malformed one.

StockoutDecisionRow.title: StockoutDecisionRow
StockoutDecisionRow.description:
A stockout row enriched with the item-site's current decision.

``decision`` is the item-site's current decision from
``stockout_decisions`` (the latest row by ``decided_at``, ``id``
breaking ties — the same row ``GET /api/stockout/decisions``
reports as current) with every stored column, or null when the
item-site has none.  ``decision_lapsed`` is true only for a current
dismissal that the row has outgrown: the row's ``p_stockout``
exceeds the decision's ``p_stockout`` by at least 0.10.  A snooze
never lapses, and neither does anything else (accepted decisions,
or no decision at all).

StockoutProposalBucket.title: StockoutProposalBucket
StockoutProposalBucket.description:
One remedy kind's two counts among the current accepted
stockout decisions: the decisions proposed the kind and the
decisions that chose it.

StockoutProposalCounts.title: StockoutProposalCounts
StockoutProposalCounts.description:
The stored remedy proposals of the current accepted stockout
decisions.

StockoutRemedy.title: StockoutRemedy
StockoutRemedy.description:
The one remedy proposed for a stockout row.

``kind`` is the remedy's kind — one of the stockout decision's own
action values (``expedite``, ``transfer`` or ``raise_order``).
The other keys carry that kind's candidate for the row's
item-site: the expedite line's ``order_type``, ``order_nbr``,
``line_nbr``, ``expected_on``, ``supplier_code`` and
``supplier_name`` (``units`` the line's ``open_units``); the
transfer suggestion's ``from_site`` (``units`` its ``quantity``);
or the order plan line's ``order_by`` and its group's
``supplier_code`` and ``name`` (``units`` the line's ``quantity``).
Every key that does not apply to the kind is null, and ``reason``
is the one line of text for why the remedy fits the row.

SupplierLeadTimeStats.title: SupplierLeadTimeStats
SupplierLeadTimeStats.description: One supplier's lead time stats for an item.

SupplierOrderMinimumIn.title: SupplierOrderMinimumIn
SupplierOrderMinimumIn.description:
The body of PUT /api/supplier-order-minimums.

``source_system`` is a 1-to-64-character string, ``supplier_code``
a 1-to-255-character string — neither with edge white space, a
control character or a lone surrogate — and ``amount`` a finite
number above 0 and at most ``AMOUNT_MAX`` inclusive.  Anything
else is rejected with a 422 before anything is written.

SupplierOrderMinimumOut.title: SupplierOrderMinimumOut
SupplierOrderMinimumOut.description: One stored supplier order minimum as served by the routes.

SupplierPerformanceEntry.title: SupplierPerformanceEntry
SupplierPerformanceEntry.description: One supplier's on-time and lead-time performance in the window.

SupplierPerformanceResponse.title: SupplierPerformanceResponse
SupplierPerformanceResponse.description: Per-supplier performance for the window ending on as_of.

SupplierResponse.title: SupplierResponse
SupplierResponse.description: Response model for a stored supplier row.

SupplierRiskEntry.title: SupplierRiskEntry
SupplierRiskEntry.description: One supplier's risk signs over the 730-day window.

SupplierRiskResponse.title: SupplierRiskResponse
SupplierRiskResponse.description: Per-supplier risk for the 730-day window ending on as_of.

SupplierTermsResponse.title: SupplierTermsResponse
SupplierTermsResponse.description: Response model for a stored supplier terms row.

SupplyPlanLine.title: SupplyPlanLine
SupplyPlanLine.description:
One item-site's line of the supply plan.

``position_units`` is on hand plus on order, ``reorder_point_units``
the recommendation's reorder point in whole units and
``daily_demand`` the recommendation's ``inputs.d``.  ``due_in_days``
is 0 when the position is at or below the reorder point, else the
days of demand left above it; ``order_by`` is the as-of plus the due
days and ``arrives_on`` the ``order_by`` plus the lead time in whole
days (the supplier terms' ``lead_time_days`` when set, else the
recommendation's ``inputs.lt``).  ``raw_quantity`` is the larger of
the recommended order quantity and the suggested order quantity;
``quantity``, ``adjustments`` and ``short_of_need`` are the raw
quantity fitted to the line's ``terms`` with
``app.supply.terms.fit_to_terms``.  ``value`` is the quantity times
the item-site's unit cost, rounded to cents (null without a cost),
and ``arithmetic`` is the one line of text showing the fitting steps.
``supplier_reason`` is null while the line's default supplier pick
stands, and reads ``Chosen over <name> (<Risk> risk: <signs>)``
when the ``supply_plan.prefer_lower_risk_supplier`` setting
switched the line to the lower-risk terms row — the name the
default pick's supplier name from the suppliers table, else its
code, the risk ``High`` or ``Medium``, and the signs ``late
deliveries`` and/or ``variable lead times``.

SupplyPlanResponse.title: SupplyPlanResponse
SupplyPlanResponse.description:
The supply plan as of the resolved as-of date (never null), the
lines due within ``horizon_days``, grouped by supplier — the
groups in the order of their earliest ``due_in_days``, then
``total_value`` descending, the no-supplier group last.

``line_count`` is the plan's lines overall and ``total_value`` their
values summed (0 when every line's value is null).

SupplyPlanSummaryResponse.title: SupplyPlanSummaryResponse
SupplyPlanSummaryResponse.description:
The one-page summary of the 7-day supply plan (the plan's
resolved as-of, never null).

``horizon_days`` is the plan's horizon (7); ``line_count`` and
``total_value`` are the plan's own, the way
``SupplyPlanResponse`` answers them for the same builder's
call, and ``supplier_count`` is the plan's supplier groups with
a non-null ``supplier_code`` (the no-supplier group never
counts).  ``transfer_count`` and ``transfer_value`` are the
transfer suggestions' ``suggestion_count`` and ``total_value``,
the way ``TransferSuggestionsResponse`` answers them for the
same builder's call.  ``transfers_in_flight`` is the number of
the rows ``TransferReleasePostgresRepository.list_in_flight``
returns whose ``erp_status`` is null or none of "Released",
"Completed" and "Canceled" — the rows still awaiting the ERP's
release — and ``transfers_awaiting_release`` how many of those
are at least the ``exceptions.release_approval_days`` system
setting (default 3) old by ``updated_at``, the exact cutoff
inclusive, a missing or out-of-range stored value falling back
to the registry default.

SupplyPlanSupplierGroup.title: SupplyPlanSupplierGroup
SupplyPlanSupplierGroup.description:
The plan lines of one supplier, ordered by ``due_in_days`` then
``item_code`` then ``site_code``.

``vendor_code`` and ``name`` come from the suppliers table (null
when the supplier is not stored).  ``total_value`` is the group's
lines' values summed (a line without a unit cost contributes zero)
and is 0 when every line's value is null.  ``minimum`` is the
stored order minimum of the group's (``source_system``,
``supplier_code``) pair — the pair's row of
``supplier_order_minimums``, listed once per plan build and
compared exactly as stored — and ``shortfall`` the minimum minus
the group's ``total_value`` when the total is below the minimum
and 0 when it is not; both rounded to cents half-up, the way the
lines' values are, and serialized the way ``total_value`` is.
Both are null for every group without a stored minimum — the
group without a supplier included — and are left out of the
response, exactly as a line leaves out a null
``supplier_reason``.  The lines with no supplier form a single
final group whose ``supplier_code`` and ``source_system`` are
null, spanning every source system.

SupplyPlanTerms.title: SupplyPlanTerms
SupplyPlanTerms.description:
A plan line's supplier ordering terms (null when the line has no
supplier): ``min_order_qty``, ``lot_size`` and ``max_order_qty``,
each a number or null.

SupplyPlanTopUp.title: SupplyPlanTopUp
SupplyPlanTopUp.description:
One line of the look-ahead plan taken to top up a supplier group
that is below its stored minimum: the look-ahead line's
``item_code``, ``site_code``, ``due_in_days``, ``order_by``,
``quantity``, ``unit_cost`` and ``value``, plus ``holding_cost`` —
the value held until the due date at the effective
``replenishment.holding_rate`` the recommendations use:
``value`` × ``holding_rate`` × ``due_in_days`` / 365, rounded to
two places half up.

SupplyPlanTopUpSupplier.title: SupplyPlanTopUpSupplier
SupplyPlanTopUpSupplier.description:
One supplier group of the order plan that has a stored minimum
and a shortfall above 0, in the plan's group order:
``supplier_code``, ``source_system``, ``vendor_code``, ``name``,
``minimum``, ``total_value`` and ``shortfall`` as the plan's group
has them, then the top-up — the look-ahead plan's lines of the same
supplier and source system due after the horizon with a value and
not on the excess list, taken by ``due_in_days``, then
``item_code``, then ``site_code``, each added until the sum of the
values taken is at least the shortfall, the line that reaches it
included and none after it.  ``top_up_value`` is the top-ups'
values summed (0 with none), ``reaches_minimum`` is true when
``total_value`` plus ``top_up_value`` is at least the ``minimum``
and ``still_short`` the minimum minus the two when that is above
0, else 0 — the money serialized the way the plan serializes the
group's ``total_value``, rounded to two places half up.

SupplyPlanTopUpsResponse.title: SupplyPlanTopUpsResponse
SupplyPlanTopUpsResponse.description:
The top-ups of the order plan as of the plan's resolved as-of
date (never null), for the ``horizon_days`` horizon (1 to 60,
default 7), for any signed-in user.

``lookahead_days`` is the effective
``supply_plan.top_up_lookahead_days`` setting — the stored value
rounded down to a whole number of days, else the default — and
``holding_rate`` the effective ``replenishment.holding_rate`` the
recommendations use.  ``suppliers`` is one entry per supplier group
of the ``horizon_days`` order plan that has a stored minimum and a
shortfall above 0, in the plan's group order.  Read-only.

TransferReleaseEntry.title: TransferReleaseEntry
TransferReleaseEntry.description:
One chosen transfer suggestion: the item and the two sites.

The request never carries a quantity — the quantity comes from
the suggestion the entry matches.  Any extra field is refused
with 422, like every other body in the app.

TransferReleaseGroup.title: TransferReleaseGroup
TransferReleaseGroup.description:
One (from_site, to_site) group of the transfer release plan.

``outcome``, ``reference_nbr``, ``from_warehouse_code``,
``to_warehouse_code`` and ``error`` are null in the bare plan and
in the preview with an incomplete Acumatica configuration; the
preview fills them from the client's per-order result, a confirm
from its batch — and for an ``exists`` outcome whose current plan
lines no longer match the stored snapshot of the origin, the
group keeps the outcome but not the existing order's reference
number (null) and carries the stale-lines error instead.

TransferReleaseIn.title: TransferReleaseIn
TransferReleaseIn.description:
The transfer release body.

``transfers`` is a non-empty list of up to 50 chosen transfer
suggestions — each string 1 to 64 characters without NUL bytes,
one entry per distinct suggestion (two entries with the same
(item_code, from_site, to_site) are refused) — and ``confirm``
the preview/confirm flag (default false).  Any extra field is
refused with 422, like every other body in the app; a missing
body is 422 by request validation.

TransferReleaseLine.title: TransferReleaseLine
TransferReleaseLine.description:
One line of one transfer release group, exactly as sent to
Acumatica: the item and the suggested quantity in whole units.

TransferReleasePlan.title: TransferReleasePlan
TransferReleasePlan.description:
The transfer release plan with the per-group Acumatica outcomes
on top.

``as_of`` is the as-of snapshot the current suggestions were read
at (never null), ``groups`` the (from_site, to_site) groups with
their lines in request order, and ``unreleasable`` the requested
entries that are no longer suggested or come from a source system
other than Acumatica.

TransferReleaseRow.title: TransferReleaseRow
TransferReleaseRow.description: One stored transfer_releases audit row, every column of it.

TransferReleaseUnreleasable.title: TransferReleaseUnreleasable
TransferReleaseUnreleasable.description:
One requested entry that is not released: the entry's item and
sites with the reason — no longer suggested, or a source system
other than Acumatica.

TransferSuggestion.title: TransferSuggestion
TransferSuggestion.description:
One suggested inter-site transfer.

``from_site`` gives ``quantity`` to ``to_site`` of the same item
and ``source_system``: ``quantity`` the smaller of the receiver's
remaining need and the donor's remaining surplus, in whole units,
``unit_cost`` the receiving item-site's, ``value`` the quantity
times the unit cost to cents (null without a cost),
``to_site_need`` the receiver's full need and
``from_site_surplus`` the donor's full surplus.  ``arithmetic`` is
the one line of text naming both numbers, e.g. "site 159 needs 120
(ROP 400 − position 280); site 154 holds 300 beyond ROP +
order quantity; move 120".

TransferSuggestionsResponse.title: TransferSuggestionsResponse
TransferSuggestionsResponse.description:
The transfer suggestions as of the resolved as-of date (never
null), ordered by ``value`` descending (the suggestions without a
value last), then ``item_code``.

``suggestion_count`` is the suggestions' count and ``total_value``
their values summed (0 when every suggestion's value is null).

UnreleasableItem.title: UnreleasableItem
UnreleasableItem.description: One planned order whose item-site has no supplier in history.

WithdrawalBody.title: WithdrawalBody
WithdrawalBody.description:
The body of POST /api/forecast/overrides/withdrawals.

Withdraws the current override of the period: a new
``withdrawal`` row with the stored period's dates.  A blank or
over-long reason answers 422; a withdrawal with nothing to
withdraw, or for a completed period, answers 409.

_CountBucket.title: _CountBucket
_CountBucket.description: A summary bucket that only carries a count.

app__api__decision_summary___MoneyBucket.title: _MoneyBucket
app__api__decision_summary___MoneyBucket.description:
One money-bearing summary bucket.

``count`` is the number of current decisions in the bucket,
``money`` sums their stored money (drift: ``money_at_stake``,
excess: ``money_tied_up``, stockout: ``money_at_risk``; a null
snapshot contributes nothing) and ``without_money`` counts those
null-snapshot decisions.

app__api__planner_decisions___MoneyBucke.title: _MoneyBucket
app__api__planner_decisions___MoneyBucke.description:
One money-bearing summary bucket.

``count`` is the number of current decisions in the bucket,
``money_at_stake`` sums their snapshotted ``money_at_stake``
(decisions whose snapshot is null contribute nothing) and
``without_money`` counts those null-snapshot decisions.
